jp.title: No installation Support contact or User Guide link anywhere in the new frontend
jp.body: ## Summary Every legacy JSF page carries "User Guide" and "Support" links in the site header, and "Support" opens a contact form addressed to the installation's support address. The new frontend's header has neither — it shows only Language, Add Data and the user menu when signed in, or Language and Log In when anonymous. There is no way to reach installation support, or the user guide, from anywhere in the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dataverse_header.xhtml` renders "Add Data", "Search", "User Guide" and "Support" alongside the user menu. "Support" is a command link (`headerSupportLink`) that opens the shared contact dialog (`PF('contactForm').show()`), pre-addressed to installation support rather than to a specific collection. Both links appear on every page, including the account pages, and for anonymous visitors. ### Steps to observe 1. Open the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080). 2. Observe "User Guide" and "Support" in the top-right header, on any page — including Account -> Account Information. 3. Click "Support" and observe the contact form for installation support. ## New frontend behavior `Header.tsx` renders the brand, a `LanguageSwitcher`, and then either `LoggedInHeaderActions` (Add Data + user menu) or a single OIDC "Log In" button. Nothing else. The SPA does have a contact modal, but it is the per-collection "Email Collection Contact" reached from a collection's "Contact" button — that addresses the collection's contacts, not installation support, and it is not reachable from the account pages or from a dataset. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern), signed in or not. 2. Inspect the header: only Language, Add Data and the user menu (or Log In). 3. Go to `/modern/account?tab=accountInformation` and confirm there is no Support or User Guide link anywhere on the page. ## Expected behavior The new frontend should offer an installation-level support contact and a user-guide link that are reachable from any page, as legacy's header does — so a user who is stuck, or whose account details are wrong, has a route to ask for help. ## Current behavior Absent. The only contact affordance in the SPA is the per-collection "Email Collection Contact" modal, which has a different recipient and is not available from account or dataset pages. Users have no in-app path to installation support and no link to the documentation. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy Account Information page — note "User Guide" and "Support" in the header, present on every page. ### New frontend The same page in the SPA: header has only Language, Add Data and the user menu — no Support, no User Guide. (This capture also evidences jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#21, the read-only account table.) ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml) (`headerSupportLink` opening `contactForm`, and the User Guide link), `header.support` and `header.guide` in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx) and [`LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx) — no support or guide entry; the existing contact modal is [`src/sections/shared/contact/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/shared/contact) (collection-scoped) - Missing-items entries: "Account Information - Contact Support", and the related "Contact Support" rows under Login Page, ORCID Confirmation, OAuth Login Callback and Search Results in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#21 (Account Information is read-only) and #24 (notification muting absent) are the sibling account-area gaps; a user hitting either has no support link to fall back on, which is part of why this one matters. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#10 (no Sign Up entry in the header) is the other missing header affordance. - The collection-level contact form itself is fully implemented, including its math CAPTCHA — two rows of the missing-items list about that turned out to be wrong. This issue is specifically about an *installation* support route. - No issue covering a header support or user-guide link in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "contact support", "support link", "user guide link" and "header support" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] An installation support contact is reachable from any page in the new frontend - [ ] It addresses the installation's support address, distinct from a collection's contacts - [ ] A user guide link is available from the header, as in legacy - [ ] Both are available to anonymous visitors as well as signed-in users - [ ] Covered by an automated test asserting both are present in the header

jp.title: Create-dataset form is missing the Add "Replication Data for" to Title helper
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF puts an `Add "Replication Data for" to Title` button directly beneath the Title field on the create-dataset form. It is a one-click convenience for depositors publishing replication datasets: it prefixes whatever is in the Title with "Replication Data for: ". The new frontend's create-dataset form has no such control. ## Legacy JSF behavior `datasetFieldForEditFragment.xhtml` renders the button for the `title` field whenever `DatasetPage.editMode == 'CREATE'`. It is client-side only — clicking it prepends `dataset.replicationDataFor` ("Replication Data for:") to the current title value. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Start a new dataset: Add Data -> New Dataset, or `/dataset.xhtml?ownerId=1&editMode=CREATE`. 3. Observe the `Add "Replication Data for" to Title` button under the Title field. 4. Type a title and click the button; the title becomes "Replication Data for: ". ## New frontend behavior The SPA create-dataset form (`/modern/datasets/:collectionId/create`) renders the Title field with no adjacent button. A case-insensitive search for `replication` across `src/` and `public/locales/` returns no matches, so the affordance does not exist anywhere in the SPA. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Go to `/modern/datasets/root/create`. 3. Observe the Citation Metadata section: the Title field has no "Replication Data for" helper button. ## Expected behavior The create-dataset form should offer the same one-click way to prefix the title for replication datasets — or, if the team considers the affordance obsolete, the decision should be recorded so this inventory row can be closed deliberately rather than left as a silent omission. ## Current behavior Absent. Depositors must type the "Replication Data for:" prefix by hand, which is where the legacy button existed to keep the wording consistent across an installation. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy create-dataset form: the `Add "Replication Data for" to Title` button sits directly under the Title field. <img width="870" height="897" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac3595b7-42d0-4165-8680-13785277d245" /> ### New frontend SPA create-dataset form, same collection: Title has no helper button. (Note that "Host Collection" and "Edit Host Collection" *are* present here — two neighbouring rows in the missing-items list turned out to be implemented.) <img width="870" height="897" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8d1f931-3b43-4241-a98d-7827c4880d5d" /> ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/datasetFieldForEditFragment.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/datasetFieldForEditFragment.xhtml) (the `replicationDataButton`, rendered when the field is `title` and `editMode == 'CREATE'`), `dataset.AddReplication` and `dataset.replicationDataFor` in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: no match for `replication` anywhere under `src/` or `public/locales/`; the create form is [`src/sections/create-dataset/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/create-dataset) - Missing-items entry: "Dataset Metadata - Add Replication Data Prefix" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - No issue covering this affordance was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "replication data", "replication data for" and "title prefix" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The create-dataset form offers a one-click way to prefix the title with "Replication Data for: ", or the team records a decision not to carry the affordance forward - [ ] Clicking it prepends the prefix to the current title without clearing it, and does not duplicate the prefix when clicked twice - [ ] It appears only in create mode, as in legacy - [ ] Covered by an automated test if implemented

jp.title: Notification muting (email and in-app) is absent from the new frontend
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF can let users choose which notifications they receive, separately for email and in-app delivery, from a "Notification settings" panel on the Notifications tab. **This panel is opt-in per installation: it only appears when an admin enables the `:ShowMuteOptions` database setting, which is `false` by default.** The new frontend's Notifications tab lists and dismisses notifications but has no muting controls, so on an installation that has turned muting on, users of the new frontend can't opt out of any notification type, including the emails. > [!IMPORTANT] > **You won't see this feature on a default installation.** The legacy panel is hidden unless `:ShowMuteOptions` is set to `true`. See [Enabling the feature](#enabling-the-feature-legacy-jsf) below before trying to reproduce. ## Enabling the feature (legacy JSF) Notification muting is controlled by three installation-wide **database settings**. They're stored in the `setting` table, have no admin UI, and are managed through the admin settings API (usually only reachable from localhost or with the API unblock key): | Setting | Default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `:ShowMuteOptions` | `false` | When `true`, shows the "Notification settings" panel on the Notifications tab. When unset or `false`, the panel is not rendered at all. | | `:AlwaysMuted` | empty | Comma-separated notification types (e.g. `ASSIGNROLE,REVOKEROLE`) that are always muted. Users can't turn them on. | | `:NeverMuted` | empty | Comma-separated notification types that are never muted. Users can't turn them off. | Types listed in `:AlwaysMuted` or `:NeverMuted` show in the panel as greyed-out (disabled) checkboxes. If a type appears in both, `:AlwaysMuted` wins and a warning is logged. These settings were added in Dataverse 5.11. ```bash # Enable the panel curl -X PUT -d true http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions # Optional: lock some types so they show as disabled checkboxes curl -X PUT -d 'ASSIGNROLE,REVOKEROLE' http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:AlwaysMuted curl -X PUT -d 'CREATEACC' http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:NeverMuted # Check the current value curl http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions # Revert to default (panel hidden) curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions ``` Docs: Installation Guide → [`:ShowMuteOptions`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#showmuteoptions), [`:AlwaysMuted`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#alwaysmuted), [`:NeverMuted`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#nevermuted). User Guide → [Notifications](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/user/account.html#notifications). ## Legacy JSF behavior With `:ShowMuteOptions=true`, `dataverseuser.xhtml` renders a collapsible "Notification settings" panel above the notification list. It has two multi-select checkbox groups and a "Save Changes" button: - `notification.mutedEmails`: "Select the email notifications you wish to receive:" - `notification.mutedNotifications`: "Select the in-app notifications you wish to receive:" Unchecking a type mutes that notification for that delivery channel. Users can also manage the same preferences through the API: `GET /api/notifications/mutedEmails`, `PUT`/`DELETE /api/notifications/mutedEmails/{typeName}`, and the same endpoints for `mutedNotifications`. ### Steps to observe 1. Enable the setting as a superuser: `curl -X PUT -d true http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions` (see [Enabling the feature](#enabling-the-feature-legacy-jsf)). 2. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 3. Go to Account → Notifications (`/dataverseuser.xhtml?selectTab=notifications`). 4. Expand "Notification settings". 5. You should see the two checkbox groups for email and in-app notification types. Uncheck one and click "Save Changes" to mute it. ## New frontend behavior The SPA Notifications tab (`/modern/account?tab=notifications`) shows "Displaying 1 - N of N Notifications", each row with a dismiss (X) control, plus a "Clear All Notifications" action. There is no settings panel and no muting UI, whatever the value of `:ShowMuteOptions`. A case-insensitive search for `mute` across `src/sections/account/notifications-section/` and `public/locales/en/account.json` finds nothing. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Enable `:ShowMuteOptions` on the backend as above. 2. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 3. Open the user menu and choose "Notifications" (or go to `/modern/account?tab=notifications`). 4. You'll see the notification list with dismiss and "Clear All Notifications", and no notification-settings or muting control anywhere on the tab. ## Expected behavior When the installation has `:ShowMuteOptions=true`, users should be able to choose, per notification type, whether they get it by email and whether it appears in-app, the same way legacy's two checkbox groups work. The choice should be saved to their account. Types locked by `:AlwaysMuted` / `:NeverMuted` should be shown but not editable. When `:ShowMuteOptions` is false (the default), no muting UI should be shown, which matches legacy. ## Current behavior The SPA has no muting. On an installation with muting enabled, users can only dismiss notifications after they arrive. They can't stop unwanted notification emails without going back to the legacy JSF page or using the API. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF ### New frontend SPA Notifications tab: list with per-row dismiss and "Clear All Notifications", no notification-settings or muting panel. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: - [`src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml` L65–100](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml#L65-L100): the panel, gated by `jsf:rendered="#{settingsWrapper.showMuteOptions}"` - [`SettingsWrapper.java` L260–262](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/SettingsWrapper.java#L260-L262): `isShowMuteOptions()` defaults to `false`; also `isAlwaysMuted` / `isNeverMuted` - [`SettingsServiceBean.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/settings/SettingsServiceBean.java): `ShowMuteOptions`, `AlwaysMuted`, `NeverMuted` keys - [`DataverseUserPage.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/authorization/providers/builtin/DataverseUserPage.java): `toReceiveEmails`, `toReceiveNotifications`, `isDisabled` - API: [`api/Notifications.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/api/Notifications.java): `/api/notifications/mutedEmails[/{typeName}]` and `/api/notifications/mutedNotifications[/{typeName}]` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx) and [`NotificationsHelper.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsHelper.tsx): no muting, and no `mute` strings in `public/locales/en/account.json` - Missing-items entries: "Notifications - Manage Muted Email Notifications" and "Notifications - Manage Muted In-App Notifications" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#21 (Account Information is read-only) is the related gap in the same account area. Both are about account self-service that the SPA shows but doesn't let the user change. - No issue covering notification muting in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc. Searched "muted notifications", "notification settings", "mute" and "notification preferences" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The notification settings UI is shown only when `:ShowMuteOptions` is `true` and is hidden by default - [ ] The Notifications tab offers per-type control over which notifications the user receives by email - [ ] It offers the same control for in-app notifications, separately from email - [ ] Types listed in `:AlwaysMuted` / `:NeverMuted` are shown as disabled and can't be changed - [ ] Choices are saved to the user's account and still show after a reload - [ ] Muting a type stops the email and/or the in-app entry for that type, depending on which channel was muted - [ ] Existing list, dismiss and "Clear All Notifications" behavior is unchanged - [ ] An automated test checks that a muted type is saved and that the UI is hidden when `:ShowMuteOptions` is false

jp.title: Publish-blocked warnings are incomplete: two unpublished generations and collection publish are not handled
jp.body: ## Summary The new frontend handles the simple publish-blocked case correctly — a dataset whose immediate parent collection is unpublished gets legacy's exact "Would you like to publish both right now?" prompt. But it misses the other two cases legacy distinguishes: when **two generations** of ancestors are unpublished it still offers to publish "both", naming only the immediate parent; and when **a collection** whose parent is unpublished is published, the SPA shows a generic confirmation with no warning at all. ## Legacy JSF behavior Legacy has three distinct messages: | Case | Legacy string | | --- | --- | | Dataset, parent unpublished, user can publish it | `dataset.mayNotPublish.both`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} is published. Would you like to publish both right now?" | | Dataset, **two** generations unpublished | `dataset.mayNotPublish.twoGenerations`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} **and {1}** are published." | | Dataset, parent must be published by someone else | `dataset.mayNotPublish.administrator`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} is published by its administrator." | And for collections: `dataverse.publish.failed` ("Cannot publish dataverse.") with `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` — "This dataverse cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published." ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Create an unpublished collection inside another unpublished collection, and a dataset inside the inner one. 3. Attempt to publish that dataset and observe the two-generations message naming both ancestors. 4. Attempt to publish the inner collection and observe the "cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published" notice. ## New frontend behavior **Two generations (dataset).** With `Root > QA Test Collection (unpublished) > Gap Review Subcollection 184 (unpublished) > dataset`, the SPA's Publish Dataset modal says only "This dataset cannot be published until **Gap Review Subcollection 184** is published. Would you like to publish both right now?" — the `.both` variant. It names one ancestor and offers to publish "both", although two ancestors are unpublished, so accepting cannot succeed as described. **Collection.** Publishing `Gap Review Subcollection 184`, whose parent `QA Test Collection` is unpublished, opens a Publish Collection modal reading only "Are you sure you want to publish your collection? Once you do so it must remain published." — no mention that the parent is unpublished and no equivalent of legacy's blocked-publish notice. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open the dataset at `/modern/datasets?persistentId=doi:10.5072/FK2/SSQN4W&version=DRAFT` (inside two unpublished collections). 3. Publish Dataset -> Publish, and observe the single-ancestor "publish both" wording. 4. Open `/modern/collections/gap-review-sub-184` and click Publish; observe the generic confirmation with no unpublished-parent warning. ## Expected behavior - A dataset with more than one unpublished ancestor should say so and name them, rather than offering to publish "both". - A dataset whose parent can only be published by someone else should say that, as legacy's `administrator` variant does. - Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished should warn, and either offer to publish the chain or explain why it cannot proceed — not present a plain confirmation. ## Current behavior Only the single-parent dataset case is handled. The other cases either show misleading wording (two generations) or no warning at all (collection), so a user can confirm an action whose stated effect is wrong. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Not screenshotted: reproducing these states in legacy means publishing collections, which permanently changes install data, and the legacy flow was deliberately left untouched. The three dataset variants and the collection notice are quoted verbatim from `Bundle.properties` above. ### New frontend Two unpublished generations (`Root > QA Test Collection > Gap Review Subcollection 184 > dataset`), yet the modal names only the immediate parent and offers to publish "both": Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished — a generic confirmation with no warning: ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: `dataset.mayNotPublish.both`, `dataset.mayNotPublish.twoGenerations`, `dataset.mayNotPublish.administrator`, `dataverse.publish.failed` and `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` in [`Bundle.properties`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/publish-dataset/PublishDatasetModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/publish-dataset/PublishDatasetModal.tsx) and [`PublishDatasetMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/PublishDatasetMenu.tsx); the collection side in [`src/sections/collection/publish-collection/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/collection/publish-collection) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Publish Blocked - Two Generations Unpublished" and "Dataverse Page - Blocked Publish Notice" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - The sibling row "Dataset Page - Publish Blocked - Parent Unpublished" is **not** a gap: the SPA reproduces legacy's `.both` message word for word. Only the two-generations and collection variants are missing. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#22 (curation status stubs) is the other finding from the same dataset publish menu. - No issue covering these publish-blocked variants was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "publish blocked", "cannot be published", "publish both" and "unpublished parent" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A dataset with two or more unpublished ancestors reports all of them and does not offer a "publish both" action that cannot succeed - [ ] A dataset whose ancestor must be published by another user gets the administrator variant of the message - [ ] Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished warns before the confirmation, matching legacy's blocked-publish notice - [ ] The existing single-parent dataset case keeps its current wording and behavior - [ ] Covered by automated tests for the two-generations and collection cases

jp.title: Change/Remove Curation Status renders its labels but every option opens the Not Implemented placeholder
jp.body: ## Summary This installation configures curation labels, and the new frontend correctly renders them: the dataset "Publish Dataset" menu shows a "Change Curation Status" submenu listing Author Contacted, Privacy Review, Awaiting Paper Publication, Final Approval and "Remove Current Status". Selecting any of them opens the "Not Implemented" modal instead of applying the status, so a curator cannot set, change or clear a dataset's curation status from the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior With curation labels configured, a curator can set a draft dataset's curation status from the dataset page, change it to another allowed label, or remove it. Legacy reports the outcome ("Curation Status Changed", "Curation Status is now \"{0}\"", "Curation Status Removed") and rejects invalid attempts with specific messages — label not allowed, status unchanged, labeling disabled, or the version already released (status can only be set on drafts). ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a **draft** dataset. 3. Set a curation status from the allowed labels, confirm the "Curation Status is now ..." confirmation, then remove it again. ## New frontend behavior `ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx` reads the allowed labels from the `ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_STATUSES` setting and renders one item per label plus "Remove Current Status" — but every item is wired to the same handler: ```tsx const handleItemClick = (event: React.MouseEvent) => { event.stopPropagation() showModal() // useNotImplementedModal } ``` So the submenu is fully populated and looks functional, but each selection opens the "Not Implemented" modal. There is no curation-status history view either. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a draft dataset — this review used `doi:10.5072/FK2/Q9LZAD`. 3. Open the "Publish Dataset" dropdown and hover/open "Change Curation Status". 4. Select any label, for example "Privacy Review". 5. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal; the dataset's curation status is unchanged. ## Expected behavior A curator should be able to set a draft dataset's curation status to any allowed label, change it, and remove it from the new frontend, with the resulting status visible on the dataset and the legacy rejection cases handled (label not allowed, no change, labeling disabled, version already released). The status history should also be viewable, as legacy records it. ## Current behavior The submenu is present and correctly populated from configuration, which makes it look implemented, but every option opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Nothing is applied and no history is shown. This is more misleading than an absent control, because the labels render correctly. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Not screenshotted: setting a curation status changes real dataset state, and the legacy flow was left untouched deliberately. The behavior is established from the `dataset.curationstatus.*` bundle keys (`header`="Curation Status Changed", `info`="Curation Status is now \"{0}\"", `removed`="Curation Status Removed", plus the four failure cases) and from the fact that this installation's labels are configured — the SPA reads and displays them, as the screenshots below show. ### New frontend The populated "Change Curation Status" submenu on a draft dataset: Author Contacted, Privacy Review, Awaiting Paper Publication, Final Approval, and Remove Current Status. Selecting "Privacy Review" opens the "Not Implemented" modal, with the submenu still visible behind it. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: `dataset.curationstatus.*` keys in [`Bundle.properties`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties); API: `/api/datasets/$id/curationStatus` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx) (every item calls `showModal()`), [`src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Change Curation Status", "Remove Curation Status" and "View Curation Status History" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#18, #19 and #20 are the other dataset-level controls stubbed with the same `NotImplementedModal`. Same pattern, different features. - The sibling "Submit for Review" control is stubbed the same way (`SubmitForReviewButton.tsx` has `onClick={showModal}`), but it only renders for a user who can update and **not** publish a dataset, so it could not be exercised with the single superuser account available here. Worth folding into the same work. - No issue covering curation-status management in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "curation status", "external status", "curation label" and "submit for review" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting a curation label applies it to the draft dataset instead of opening the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] The applied status is visible on the dataset - [ ] "Remove Current Status" clears it - [ ] Rejections are surfaced clearly: label not allowed, status unchanged, labeling disabled, and version already released - [ ] Curation status history can be viewed - [ ] The submenu only appears for users permitted to curate, and only for draft versions - [ ] Covered by automated tests for setting and removing a status

jp.title: Account Information is read-only in the new frontend: no edit, password change or email verification
jp.body:
## Summary Legacy JSF lets a user manage their own account: edit their name, email, affiliation and position, change their password, and re-send the email-verification message when their address is unverified. The new frontend's Account Information tab is a **read-only table** — it displays the same fields but offers no edit, no password change and no email verification. The SPA source marks all three as TODO. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dataverseuser.xhtml` (Account Information tab) shows Username, Given Name, Family Name, Email, Affiliation and Position, with an "Edit Account" dropdown offering **Edit Account Information** and **Change Password**. An unverified address is flagged "Not Verified" beside a **Send Verification Email** button. The edit form saves or cancels. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Go to Account -> Account Information (`/dataverseuser.xhtml?selectTab=accountInfo`). 3. Observe the "Edit Account" dropdown and, next to the email, the "Not Verified" flag with "Send Verification Email". 4. Choose Edit Account Information, change a field and save or cancel; choose Change Password and set a new one. ## New frontend behavior `AccountInfoSection.tsx` renders a plain table of the session user's fields and nothing else. Its first lines are the SPA authors' own TODOs: ```tsx // TODO - Add verified email icon // TODO - Edit account information // TODO - Change password export const AccountInfoSection = () => { const { user } = useSession() return ({/* username, givenName, familyName, email, affiliation, position */}
) } ``` `public/locales/en/account.json` correspondingly has keys only for the field labels under `info.*` — there are no strings for editing, saving, cancelling, password change or email verification. The Notifications section likewise has no muting controls (no `mute` reference anywhere in `src/sections/account/notifications-section/`). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Open the user menu and choose "Account Information". 3. Observe the fields rendered as static text, with no Edit, Change Password or email-verification control anywhere on the tab. ## Expected behavior A user should be able to edit their own account details, change their password, and trigger email verification from the new frontend, with the unverified state visibly flagged — matching the legacy Account Information tab. ## Current behavior Read-only. The SPA shows account details but provides no way to change them; password changes and email verification must be done in the legacy JSF UI (or, for OIDC-backed accounts, in the identity provider). ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy Account Information tab: the "Edit Account" dropdown (Edit Account Information / Change Password) and the email flagged "Not Verified" with a "Send Verification Email" button. ### New frontend ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseUserPage.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseUserPage.java) (edit account, change password, `sendVerificationEmail`) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/account/account-info-section/AccountInfoSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/account-info-section/AccountInfoSection.tsx) (read-only, with the TODOs quoted above), `public/locales/en/account.json` (`info.*` labels only), [`src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx) (no muting) - Missing-items entries: "Account Information" rows (Edit Account Information, Save Account Changes, Change Password, Save New Password, Cancel Edit, Verify Email Address) in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#712 ("SPA User Menu Navigation Breaks After Visiting Account Information", closed) touched this same tab but concerned navigation, not editing. Not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1020 ("Redesign the Dataverse account creation workflow to encourage users to add ORCIDs") and #1022 ("Let a user add a ROR to describe their affiliation during account creation") both propose changes to account *creation*; they assume account details are editable. Related, not duplicates. - For OIDC-backed installations, password change belongs to the identity provider (see IQSS/dataverse-frontend#652, closed, which established that the SPA delegates login to a themed Keycloak page). Scoping this issue should decide whether "Change Password" is in scope for the SPA at all, or whether it should link out to the provider. - No issue covering editable account information in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "edit account information SPA", "change password SPA", "account information" and "verify email SPA" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A user can edit their given name, family name, email, affiliation and position from the Account Information tab - [ ] Changes are saved, and Cancel discards them without saving - [ ] An unverified email address is visibly flagged and a verification email can be re-sent - [ ] A password change is offered for builtin accounts, or the tab links to the identity provider where that is the correct owner — whichever the maintainers decide, the current silent absence is resolved - [ ] Covered by automated tests for editing and saving account details

jp.title: Dataset and file permissions management opens placeholder in the new frontend
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a dataset curator manage who can access a dataset and its restricted files: assign and remove roles on the dataset, and — on a separate file-permissions screen — grant or reject file access requests (individually or in bulk), revoke granted access, and review the request history. In the new frontend the dataset Edit menu still shows a "Permissions" submenu with "Dataset" and "File" entries, but both are wired to the shared not-implemented handler, so neither screen is reachable. ## Legacy JSF behavior Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> **Dataset** opens `permissions-manage.xhtml`, which lists the users and groups with access, their roles, an "Assign Roles to Users/Groups" action and a "Remove Assigned Role" action per row, plus a Roles panel. Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> **File** opens `permissions-manage-files.xhtml`, which lists restricted files and pending access requests with: Grant Access, Grant All / Grant Selected, Reject All / Reject Selected, Revoke access for an already-granted user, toggles to show deleted files and the access-request history, and a download of the file-permissions history. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a dataset, then Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> Dataset (or `/permissions-manage.xhtml?id=`). 3. Observe the Users/Groups table with "Assign Roles to Users/Groups" and "Remove Assigned Role". 4. Choose Permissions -> File (`/permissions-manage-files.xhtml?id=`) and observe the file-access request and grant controls. ## New frontend behavior `EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx` renders the submenu and attaches the not-implemented handler to the whole dropdown: ```tsx {dataset.permissions.canManageDatasetPermissions && ( {t('...permissions.dataset')})} {dataset.permissions.canManageFilesPermissions && ( {t('...permissions.file')})} ``` So selecting either "Dataset" or "File" opens the "Not Implemented" modal. There is no dataset-permissions or file-permissions route or component in the SPA. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a dataset you can administer and open the "Edit Dataset" dropdown. 3. Open the "Permissions" submenu and select "Dataset" (then repeat for "File"). 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal in both cases. ## Expected behavior A dataset curator should be able to manage dataset role assignments in the new frontend (list, assign, remove) and handle file access requests (grant or reject individually and in bulk, revoke granted access, review and export the request history, and optionally show deleted files) — gated on `canManageDatasetPermissions` and `canManageFilesPermissions` respectively. ## Current behavior Both submenu entries are present but non-functional — they open the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Dataset access administration requires leaving the SPA for the legacy JSF pages. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy dataset Permissions page for a draft test dataset: Users/Groups with their roles, "Assign Roles to Users/Groups", and "Remove Assigned Role" per assignment. **Scope note:** the *file* permissions screen could not be shown with meaningful content. It lists restricted files and access requests, and no data file can exist in this install — its only storage driver is `s3`, pointed at AWS with placeholder credentials and no S3 service running, so every upload fails. The file-side controls are therefore described from `permissions-manage-files.xhtml` rather than screenshotted. ### New frontend The shared "Not Implemented" modal that both entries open. **Note:** this capture was taken from the *collection* Edit dropdown, which uses the same `NotImplementedModal` component that `EditDatasetPermissionsMenu`'s `showModal` triggers. The SPA session expired partway through this review and re-authenticating requires a password, so a capture from the dataset Permissions submenu specifically is pending; the wiring is quoted above. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/permissions-manage.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/permissions-manage.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/permissions-manage-files.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/permissions-manage-files.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/roles-assign.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/roles-assign.xhtml) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx) (`onSelect={showModal}`); no permissions route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Manage Dataset Permissions", "Dataset Page - Manage File Permissions" and the nine "Manage File Permissions" rows in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#2 (collection "Manage Permissions" opens placeholder) is the collection-level counterpart, stubbed the same way. Same pattern, different object. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#19 (Private/Preview URL creation) and #18 (Thumbnails + Widgets) are sibling entries in the same dataset Edit menu. - IQSS/dataverse#12076 ("Dataverse linking still requires superuser despite introduction of LinkDataverse permission") concerns permission semantics rather than this UI. Not a duplicate. - No issue covering SPA dataset or file permission management was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "dataset permissions SPA", "file access requests", "grant file access" and "manage permissions" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Permissions -> Dataset opens a role-assignment view instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] Roles can be assigned to users and groups, and existing assignments removed - [ ] Permissions -> File opens a file-access view listing restricted files and pending requests - [ ] Access requests can be granted and rejected individually and in bulk - [ ] Granted access can be revoked - [ ] The access-request history can be reviewed and exported, and deleted files optionally shown - [ ] The two entries respect `canManageDatasetPermissions` and `canManageFilesPermissions` - [ ] Covered by automated tests for assigning a role and for granting and rejecting a file access request

jp.title: Dataset Private/Preview URL creation opens placeholder in the new frontend
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a dataset editor create a shareable review link for an unpublished draft — called "Preview URL" in 6.11 (formerly "Private URL") — then copy it or disable it, with an anonymized variant when the installation configures anonymized fields. In the new frontend the dataset Edit menu still lists "Private URL", but the entry is wired to the shared not-implemented handler, so no review link can be created, copied or disabled. ## Legacy JSF behavior Edit Dataset -> "Preview URL" opens the "Unpublished Dataset Preview URL" dialog. For a draft it offers **Create General Preview URL**; once created it shows the generated `previewurl.xhtml?token=...` link with **Copy to Clipboard** and **Disable General Preview URL**. For a published version it refuses with "Preview URL can only be used with unpublished versions of datasets." Only one Preview URL can be active per draft. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open an **unpublished draft** dataset (this review used `doi:10.5072/FK2/8PW3WO`). 3. Open the "Edit Dataset" dropdown and select "Preview URL". 4. Click "Create General Preview URL" and observe the generated link with "Copy to Clipboard" and "Disable General Preview URL". ## New frontend behavior `EditDatasetMenu.tsx` lists the entry as `EditDatasetMenuItems.PRIVATE_URL`, shown when the user can manage dataset or file permissions, and its handler is: ```tsx if (eventKey === EditDatasetMenuItems.PRIVATE_URL) { showModal() return } ``` So it opens the "Not Implemented" modal. The SPA *can consume* a preview URL token (`getDatasetByPrivateUrlToken`, anonymized view in `DatasetFactory.tsx`), but it provides no way to create, copy or disable one. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open an unpublished draft dataset you can edit and open the "Edit Dataset" dropdown. 3. Select "Private URL". 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal. No link is created and none can be copied or disabled. ## Expected behavior A user who can manage dataset permissions should be able to create a preview/private URL for a draft from the new frontend, copy it, and disable it — plus create the anonymized variant where the installation enables it — and be told clearly that the feature applies only to unpublished versions. ## Current behavior The menu entry is present but non-functional — it opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Creating a review link requires leaving the SPA for the legacy JSF page, even though the SPA already understands the resulting token. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Unpublished Dataset Preview URL" dialog on a draft dataset after creating the link: the generated `previewurl.xhtml?token=...` URL with "Copy to Clipboard" and "Disable General Preview URL". **Scope note:** only the "General Preview" option appeared. The anonymized variant depends on `:AnonymizedFieldTypeNames`, which is not set in this install, so the anonymized flow could not be exercised and is described from source. ### New frontend The shared "Not Implemented" modal that this entry opens. **Note:** this capture was taken from the *collection* Edit dropdown, which uses the same `NotImplementedModal` component that `EditDatasetMenu`'s `showModal()` triggers. The SPA session expired partway through this review and re-authenticating requires a password, so a capture from the dataset Edit menu specifically is pending; the wiring is quoted above. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataset.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataset.xhtml) (`datasetForm:privateUrl` dialog), [`src/main/webapp/previewurl.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/previewurl.xhtml), `dataset.privateurl.*` keys in `Bundle.properties`; API: `/api/datasets/$id/privateUrl` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetMenu.tsx) (`PRIVATE_URL -> showModal()`); consumption side exists in [`src/sections/dataset/DatasetFactory.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/DatasetFactory.tsx) and `getDatasetByPrivateUrlToken` - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Create / Create Anonymized / Disable / Copy Private URL" and the "Private URL" and "Preview URL" rows in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1025 ("Dataset Page: Getting Dataset with Preview URL results in 404 error", open) is the *consumption* side of the same feature in the SPA — opening a preview URL fails. This issue is about *creating* one. Complementary, not a duplicate; both are needed for the feature to work end to end. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#18 (dataset Thumbnails + Widgets) is a sibling entry in the same dataset Edit menu, stubbed by the same handler. - No issue covering preview/private URL *creation* in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "private url SPA", "preview url SPA", "anonymized access" and "private url" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting the Private/Preview URL entry opens a working dialog instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] A general preview URL can be created for an unpublished draft - [ ] The created URL is shown and can be copied in one action - [ ] The URL can be disabled, after which it stops working - [ ] Where the installation enables anonymized fields, the anonymized variant can also be created - [ ] Attempting it on a published version explains that the feature applies only to unpublished versions - [ ] Only users who can manage dataset permissions see the entry - [ ] Covered by automated tests for create, copy and disable

jp.title: Collection "Dataset Templates" management opens placeholder instead of the templates page
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a collection administrator manage dataset templates — create a template of pre-filled metadata, set it as the collection default (or unset it), add per-field instructions, copy, edit and delete templates. In the new frontend the collection Edit menu still lists "Dataset Templates", but the entry is wired to the shared not-implemented handler, so none of it is reachable. ## Legacy JSF behavior `manage-templates.xhtml` lists the collection's templates with a "Create Dataset Template" button and per-template actions: make default / unset default, edit, copy ("so you do not have to start over"), and delete. Templates are authored on `template.xhtml`, where metadata values and per-field instructions are entered and saved. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Navigate to a collection, open the "Edit" dropdown and choose "Dataset Templates", or go to `/manage-templates.xhtml?dataverseId=1`. 3. Observe the "Manage Dataset Templates" page with "Create Dataset Template" and the guidance panel. 4. With a template created, observe the make-default / unset-default, edit, copy and delete actions, and the Save Changes action on the template editor. ## New frontend behavior The collection Edit dropdown lists "Dataset Templates", but in `EditCollectionDropdown.tsx` that item is a `DropdownButtonItem` with `onClick={handleNotImplementedClick}`, which opens `NotImplementedModal`. There is no templates route, component or i18n beyond the menu label, and no template editor. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Navigate to a collection and open the "Edit" dropdown. 3. Select "Dataset Templates". 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal. No template management appears. ## Expected behavior Selecting "Dataset Templates" should open a template-management view in the SPA equivalent to the legacy page: list templates, create one with pre-filled metadata values and per-field instructions, set or unset the collection default, copy, edit, save and delete — and the chosen template should then be offered when creating a dataset in that collection. ## Current behavior The menu entry is present but non-functional — it opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal. The only route to template management is to leave the SPA for the legacy JSF page. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Manage Dataset Templates" page for the root collection, with the "Create Dataset Template" action and the guidance describing default-setting, copying and deleting. ### New frontend The collection Edit dropdown listing "Dataset Templates" (alongside Dataset Guestbooks, Permissions and Groups) with the shared "Not Implemented" modal open. **Note:** all of those entries are wired to the same `handleNotImplementedClick` / `NotImplementedModal` in `EditCollectionDropdown.tsx`; in this capture the modal was triggered from that same menu. The SPA session expired partway through this review and re-authenticating requires a password, so a capture triggered specifically from the "Dataset Templates" entry is pending — the wiring is identical and visible in the source linked below. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/manage-templates.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/manage-templates.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/template.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/template.xhtml), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/TemplatePage.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/TemplatePage.java) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx) renders `editCollection.datasetTemplates` with `onClick={handleNotImplementedClick}`; no templates route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entries: "Manage Templates - Make Default Template", "Manage Templates - Unset Default Template", "Template (Create/Edit) - Save Template Changes" and "Dataset Metadata - View/Edit Field Instructions (template)" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#16 (Dataset Guestbooks management), #6 (Theme + Widgets), #2 (Manage Permissions) and #3 (Manage Groups) are the sibling entries in the same collection Edit dropdown, all stubbed by the same handler. - Legacy notes on its own templates page that hiding/requiring metadata fields is configured on the collection's General Information page, which the SPA *does* implement (`Route.EDIT_COLLECTION`) — useful boundary when scoping this work. - No issue covering SPA dataset-template management was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "dataset template", "manage templates", "default template" and "template SPA" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting "Dataset Templates" opens a template-management view instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] Existing templates are listed, showing which is the collection default - [ ] A template can be created with pre-filled metadata values and per-field instructions - [ ] A template can be set as the collection default and unset again - [ ] A template can be copied, edited, saved and deleted - [ ] A template chosen for the collection is offered when creating a dataset there - [ ] The entry is only offered to users permitted to edit the collection - [ ] Covered by automated tests for creating a template and for setting/unsetting the default

The SPA session expired partway through this review and re-authenticating requires a password, so a capture triggered specifically from the "Dataset Guestbooks" entry is pending — the wiring is identical and visible in the source linked below. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/manage-guestbooks.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/manage-guestbooks.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/guestbook.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/guestbook.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/guestbook-responses.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/guestbook-responses.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/guestbook-preview-popup-fragment.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/guestbook-preview-popup-fragment.xhtml) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx) renders `editCollection.datasetGuestbooks` with `onClick={handleNotImplementedClick}`; no guestbooks route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entries: "Manage Guestbooks" rows (Delete Guestbook, Confirm Delete Guestbook, Cancel Delete Guestbook), "Guestbook Preview Dialog - Edit Guestbook from Preview" and "Guestbook Responses - Sort Responses Table" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#6 (Theme + Widgets), #2 (Manage Permissions) and #3 (Manage Groups) are the sibling entries in the same collection Edit dropdown, all stubbed by the same handler. Same pattern, different features. - The SPA does implement *assigning* an existing guestbook to a dataset (`src/sections/edit-dataset-terms/edit-guestbook/`), so the dataset-side consumption exists while collection-side management does not — worth noting when scoping. - No issue covering SPA guestbook management was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "guestbook", "manage guestbooks", "guestbook responses" and "guestbook SPA" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting "Dataset Guestbooks" opens a guestbook-management view instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] Existing guestbooks are listed with their enabled state and response count - [ ] A guestbook can be created, choosing which account fields to collect and adding custom questions - [ ] A guestbook can be enabled, disabled, edited and copied - [ ] A guestbook can be deleted behind a confirmation that can be cancelled - [ ] Collected responses can be viewed and sorted - [ ] The entry is only offered to users permitted to edit the collection - [ ] Covered by automated tests for creating, editing and deleting a guestbook

jp.title: Superuser reindex tools (Index All / Check Status) are absent from the new frontend
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF gives superusers a small operations page with "Index All" and "Check Status of Index All" — a way to trigger a full Solr reindex of the installation and then see its progress from the browser. The new frontend has no equivalent page or control, so a reindex can only be triggered via the API. ## Legacy JSF behavior `superuser.xhtml` renders two buttons, "Index All" and "Check Status of Index All", with a status line below ("No status available" until a reindex has run). "Index All" kicks off a full reindex; "Check Status of Index All" reports progress without re-triggering it. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as a superuser (`dataverseAdmin`). 2. Navigate to `/superuser.xhtml`. 3. Observe the "Index All" and "Check Status of Index All" buttons and the status line. ## New frontend behavior There is no reindex or index-status UI in the SPA. Searching `src/` and `public/locales/` for `indexAll`, "index all" and related terms returns nothing, and `Route.enum.ts` has no superuser-operations route. Any such path falls through to the SPA's 404 page. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Note there is no dashboard or superuser-tools entry in the header (see jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#5). 3. jp.title: Site header has no Sign Up entry for anonymous visitors in the new frontend
jp.body:
## Summary With self-registration enabled (`:AllowSignUp=yes`), the legacy JSF site header shows an anonymous visitor both "Sign Up" and "Log In". The new frontend's header shows only "Log In", which starts the OIDC flow. A first-time visitor to the SPA has no visible way to create an account from the header — registration is only reachable after clicking Log In (via a sign-up link in the Keycloak login theme) or from a Request Access modal. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dataverse_header.xhtml` renders, for an unauthenticated visitor, a "Sign Up" item pointing at the account-creation form followed by a "Log In" item. Both sit in the top-right navigation. ### Steps to observe 1. Open the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as an anonymous visitor (no session). 2. Observe "Sign Up" and "Log In" in the top-right of the header. 3. Click "Sign Up" and observe the Create Account form at `/dataverseuser.xhtml?editMode=CREATE`. The anonymous server-rendered header contains both links: ```html
  • Sign Up
  • Log In
    • ``` ## New frontend behavior `Header.tsx` renders, for an anonymous visitor, only a `LanguageSwitcher` and a single "Log In" button wired to `oidcLogin` — there is no sign-up affordance in the header at all: ```tsx {user ? ( ) : ( )} ``` The SPA does define sign-up routes, but neither is reachable from the header: `Route.SIGN_UP` (`/sign-up`) is used only by `SessionProvider` for the OIDC "valid token but not linked account" case, and `Route.SIGN_UP_JSF` is referenced only from `RequestAccessModal`. A sign-up link back to the JSF form also exists inside the bundled Keycloak login theme (`src/keycloak-theme/login/components/SignInNotice.tsx`), so registration is reachable *after* clicking Log In. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) while logged out. 2. Observe the header: only "Language" and "Log In" are shown. 3. Confirm there is no Sign Up, Register or Create Account control anywhere on the page. ## Expected behavior When self-registration is enabled for the installation, an anonymous visitor to the new frontend should have a visible way to create an account from the header, as legacy does — whether that links to the JSF create-account form, the SPA's own sign-up route, or the identity provider's registration page. ## Current behavior The header offers only "Log In". Registration is reachable only indirectly: after starting the OIDC flow, via the sign-up link in the Keycloak login theme, or incidentally from a Request Access modal. The header never advertises it, and the SPA does not consult `:AllowSignUp` when deciding what to render. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Not screenshotted: the browser session used for this review is authenticated, and the legacy header only shows Sign Up to anonymous visitors. Re-authenticating afterwards would require entering a password, which was out of scope for this review, so the legacy evidence is the anonymous server-rendered markup quoted above (fetched without cookies), together with `dataverse_header.xhtml`. ### New frontend Modern frontend header while logged out: only "Language" and "Log In" — no Sign Up. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml) (anonymous Sign Up / Log In items), [`src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml) (`editMode=CREATE` account form), `:AllowSignUp` setting - New frontend source: [`src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx) (renders only the OIDC Log In button when anonymous), [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) (`SIGN_UP`, `SIGN_UP_JSF`), [`src/sections/session/SessionProvider.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/session/SessionProvider.tsx), `src/keycloak-theme/login/components/SignInNotice.tsx` - Missing-items entry: "Site Header - Sign Up" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#652 ("Keycloak theming - Login page", closed as completed) and #930 ("Add Warning Message to Login page", closed) establish that the SPA delegates the login page to a themed Keycloak page. That is why the other legacy login-page affordances are out of scope here; this issue is only about the header's missing sign-up entry point. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#868 ("SPA login shows 'Account not linked' for builtin users on demo; JSF login works", closed) covers builtin-user login problems in the SPA. Adjacent, not a duplicate. - No issue about a missing header sign-up entry was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "sign up SPA", "builtin users SPA login", "login page SPA", "password reset SPA" and "OIDC only login SPA" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] An anonymous visitor to the new frontend sees a sign-up entry point in the header when the installation allows self-registration - [ ] The entry point leads to a working account-creation flow - [ ] The entry point is hidden when `:AllowSignUp` is not enabled - [ ] Nothing is shown to an already-authenticated user - [ ] Covered by an automated test for the anonymous and authenticated header states

jp.title: New frontend has no 403 or 500 error pages; all non-404 failures show one generic "Oops" page
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF serves three distinct error pages, mapped by status code in `web.xml`: a 403 that tells the user they are not authorized and links them to installation support, a 500 that identifies an internal server error, and a 404. The new frontend differentiates only the 404 case; every other routing or loader failure renders one generic page reading "Oops, something went wrong..." with no status code, no indication of whether the problem is permissions or a server fault, and no support contact. ## Legacy JSF behavior `WEB-INF/web.xml` maps `403 -> /403.xhtml`, `500 -> /500.xhtml` and `404 -> /404static.xhtml`. - **403** renders "**Not Authorized** - You are not authorized to view this page. If you believe this is an error, please contact Support for assistance.", where the support name is a mailto/contact link. - **500** renders "**Internal Server Error** - An unexpected error was encountered, no more information is available." ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080). 2. Navigate to http://localhost:8080/403.xhtml and observe the Not Authorized message with its support contact link. 3. Navigate to http://localhost:8080/500.xhtml and observe the Internal Server Error message. ## New frontend behavior The SPA has exactly one differentiated error page — `NotFoundPage` at `/404` (`Route.NOT_FOUND_PAGE`), which correctly reports "We can't find the ... you're looking for." Everything else is handled by a single `errorElement`: `ErrorPage` is attached to the root route and to each child route in `src/router/routes.tsx`, and it renders only the strings from `public/locales/en/errorPage.json`: ```json { "message": { "heading": "Oops,", "errorText": "something went wrong..." }, "brandName": "Dataverse", "backToHomepage": "Back to {{brandName}} Homepage" } ``` There is no 403 route, no 500 route, and `ErrorPage` does not read the status from the route error — it ignores `useRouteError()`'s status entirely except for logging. So a permission failure and a server fault are visually indistinguishable to the user, and neither offers a support contact. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Navigate to any unknown path, for example http://localhost:8000/modern/dashboard/move-dataset, and observe that a 404 *is* handled (redirect to `/modern/404`). 3. Inspect `src/sections/Route.enum.ts` and confirm the only error route is `NOT_FOUND_PAGE = '/404'` — there is no 403 or 500 equivalent. 4. Inspect `src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx` and `public/locales/en/errorPage.json` and confirm the generic page carries no status code and no support link. ## Expected behavior A permission failure in the new frontend should render a 403-equivalent page that says the user is not authorized and points them at installation support, and an unexpected server error should render a 500-equivalent page that identifies it as a server error — rather than both collapsing into "Oops, something went wrong...". ## Current behavior Divergent, not entirely absent: the SPA handles 404 properly but has no 403 or 500 variants. Both conditions fall through to one generic error page that omits the status code, the permission-versus-server distinction, and the support contact that legacy provides on 403. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy 403 page: names the authorization problem and links to installation support. Legacy 500 page: identifies the failure as an internal server error. ### New frontend The SPA's only status-specific error page is the 404 shown below. **This is not the 403/500 path** — it is included to show that error pages exist but only for the not-found case. The generic `ErrorPage` that a 403 or 500 would produce could not be triggered on demand in a dev build, so its content is quoted above directly from `ErrorPage.tsx` and `errorPage.json` rather than screenshotted. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml) (`error-page` mappings), [`src/main/webapp/403.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/403.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/500.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/500.xhtml) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx) (generic, status-agnostic), [`src/router/routes.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/router/routes.tsx) (`errorElement: ` on every route), [`src/sections/not-found-page/NotFoundPage.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-found-page/NotFoundPage.tsx), `public/locales/en/errorPage.json` - Missing-items entries: "Error Pages - 403 Forbidden Page" and "Error Pages - 500 Internal Server Error Page" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - The sibling row "Error Pages - 404 Static Fallback Page" is **not** a gap: the SPA's `NotFoundPage` covers it. The only residual difference is that legacy's `404static.xhtml` is served by the application server while the SPA's 404 is a client-side route needing the JS bundle. - No issue covering SPA 403 or 500 error pages was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "403", "500", "error page", "forbidden" and "internal server error" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A permission failure renders a 403-equivalent page stating the user is not authorized - [ ] The 403 page offers a way to contact installation support, as legacy does - [ ] An unexpected server error renders a 500-equivalent page identifying it as a server error - [ ] The generic fallback distinguishes these cases rather than showing the same text for all failures - [ ] The existing 404 behavior is unchanged - [ ] Covered by automated tests asserting the 403 and 500 states render their respective pages

jp.title: Dashboard "Move Dataset" workflow is absent from the new frontend
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF gives superusers a "Move Dataset" page on the administrative dashboard for relocating a dataset from one collection to another: pick the dataset, pick the destination collection, submit, and confirm. The new frontend has no equivalent — no move route or component exists, and because the SPA has no dashboard at all, there is no entry point either. A superuser must return to the legacy JSF UI to move a dataset. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dashboard-movedataset.xhtml` renders two panels — "Dataset to move" with a `sourceDatasetMenu` type-ahead (by persistent ID) and "New dataverse collection host" with a `destinationDataverseMenu` type-ahead — plus "Save Changes" and "Cancel". Submitting validates the pair and raises a confirmation dialog before the move is executed. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as a superuser (`dataverseAdmin`). 2. Open the dashboard (`/dashboard.xhtml`) and click "Move Dataset" in the Data card, or go straight to `/dashboard-movedataset.xhtml?dataverseId=1`. 3. Observe the "Dataset to move" field ("Enter Dataset Persistent ID, doi:...") and the "New dataverse collection host" field ("Enter Dataverse Identifier..."). 4. Select a dataset and a destination collection, click "Save Changes", and observe the confirmation dialog before the move is applied. ## New frontend behavior There is no move functionality of any kind in the SPA. A case-insensitive search across `src/` for `moveDataverse`, `moveCollection` and `moveDataset` returns no matches, `Route.enum.ts` contains no move route, and there is no dashboard route to reach one from. Navigating to a plausible move URL falls through to the SPA's 404 page. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Note there is no dashboard entry in the header for a superuser (see jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#5). 3. Navigate directly to http://localhost:8000/modern/dashboard/move-dataset. 4. Observe the redirect to `/modern/404` — the route is not registered, so no move-dataset UI exists to permission-gate in the first place. ## Expected behavior A superuser should be able to move a dataset to a different collection from the new frontend: choose the dataset, choose the destination collection, review a confirmation of the planned move, and apply or cancel it — with the same superuser-only gating as legacy. ## Current behavior Absent. No route, no component, no menu entry, and no "Not Implemented" placeholder — there is nothing to click. The backend already exposes `POST /api/datasets/$id/move/$alias`, so only the UI is missing. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Move Dataset" dashboard page, showing the dataset type-ahead, the destination collection type-ahead, and Save Changes / Cancel. ### New frontend Modern frontend: `/modern/dashboard/move-dataset` falls through to the SPA 404 page. The route is absent from `Route.enum.ts`, so this is a missing route rather than a permission denial. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dashboard-movedataset.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dashboard-movedataset.xhtml) (`sourceDatasetMenu`, `destinationDataverseMenu`, `move` commandButton and its confirmation dialog), `dashboard.move.dataset.*` keys in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: no move route or component found — no matches for `moveDataset`/`moveCollection`/`moveDataverse` under `src/`, and no move route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entries: "Move Dataset - Search/Select Dataset to Move" and the five following rows in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#5 (SPA has no dashboard or dashboard entry point) is the blocking prerequisite — this page is reached from the dashboard in legacy. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#309 ("Add 'Move Dataverse collection' to the Move Data part of the Dashboard") is the sibling request for moving *collections* rather than datasets. Related, different object; the two would likely be built together. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#603 ("Allow forced move of dataverse datasets and collections from the Dataverse dashboard") asks for a `forceMove` option on top of this workflow. Depends on this, not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#498 ("Move datasets/collections: Add links to the dataset and collections in the alert message") refines the post-move alert. Depends on this, not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse#8269 ("admin dashboard: make the move dataset page more user-friendly") is a usability request against the legacy page. Useful input if this is rebuilt; not a duplicate. - No issue tracking the absence of a move-dataset UI in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "move dataset SPA", "move collection SPA", "move dataverse collection" and "dashboard move data" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A superuser can reach a move-dataset view in the new frontend - [ ] The view lets the user find and select the dataset to move (by persistent ID or search) - [ ] The view lets the user find and select the destination collection - [ ] Submitting shows a confirmation summarising the planned move, which can be confirmed or dismissed without moving - [ ] Confirming moves the dataset and reports success or a validation failure (for example a duplicate persistent identifier or a guestbook/template conflict) - [ ] The view is not reachable by non-superusers - [ ] Covered by an automated test for a successful move and for a rejected move
