jp.title: Collection "Theme + Widgets" opens placeholder instead of the theme/branding form
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a collection administrator brand a collection from the "Theme + Widgets" page: inherit the parent theme, upload logo / thumbnail / footer images, set header background, link and text colors, and set a tagline and website link. The new frontend keeps the "Theme + Widgets" entry in the collection Edit menu, but selecting it opens the "Not Implemented" modal — no theme form exists in the SPA, so collection branding cannot be viewed or changed there. ## Legacy JSF behavior `ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml` renders a two-tab page ("Theme" and "Widgets"). The Theme tab is bound to `themeWidgetFragment.editDv` and exposes the full branding form. It renders for any collection that has a parent, and for the root collection unless the `rootDataverseThemeDisabled` setting is on. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Navigate to a non-root collection — for example "QA Test Collection" at `/dataverse/qa-test-collection`. 3. Click the "Edit" dropdown, then "Theme + Widgets" (`/ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml?id=2`). 4. Observe the "Theme" tab with: Inherit Theme checkbox, Logo Image upload, Thumbnail Image upload, Header Colors (Background Color, Link Color, Text Color), Tagline, Website, Footer Image upload, and "Save Changes" / "Cancel". ## New frontend behavior The collection Edit dropdown still lists "Theme + Widgets", but the item is wired to the shared not-implemented handler rather than to a route: in `EditCollectionDropdown.tsx` it is a `DropdownButtonItem` with `onClick={handleNotImplementedClick}`, which opens `NotImplementedModal`. The modal offers a link back to the original JSF page as the only way to use the feature. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Navigate to the same collection at `/modern/collections/qa-test-collection`. 3. Click the "Edit" dropdown and select "Theme + Widgets". 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal: "This feature is not implemented yet in the Modern version. If you want to use this feature you can go to the original Dataverse page." No theme form is shown. ## Expected behavior Selecting "Theme + Widgets" for a collection should open a theme/branding form in the SPA equivalent to the legacy Theme tab, letting an administrator inherit the parent theme or set the collection's logo, thumbnail and footer images, header colors, tagline and website, and save those changes. ## Current behavior The menu entry is present but non-functional: it opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal instead of a theme form. There is no theme route or component in the SPA, so the only path to collection branding is to leave the SPA for the legacy JSF page. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Theme" tab for QA Test Collection, showing the full branding form (Inherit Theme, Logo Image, Thumbnail Image, Header Colors, Tagline, Website, Footer Image) and the sibling "Widgets" tab. ### New frontend Modern frontend: selecting "Theme + Widgets" from the collection Edit dropdown (visible behind the modal) opens the "Not Implemented" modal. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/themeAndWidgetsFragment.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/themeAndWidgetsFragment.xhtml) (`p:tab id="themeTab"`), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/ThemeWidgetFragment.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/ThemeWidgetFragment.java) (`initEditDv`), `dataverse.theme.*` keys in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx) renders `editCollection.themeAndWidgets` with `onClick={handleNotImplementedClick}`; [`src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx); no theme route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entry: "Theme & Widgets - View Theme Tab" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#268 ("Support collection logo image") asks for logo customization via the Native API and states the new SPA UI should retain collection logo customization. It overlaps on the logo image only, not the rest of the theme form (inherit theme, colors, tagline, website, thumbnail and footer images). Closely related — worth coordinating, but narrower than this gap. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#298 ("Dataverse collection thumbnail in addition to Logo Image as banner (SPA)") proposes a new, distinct thumbnail field on the Theme and Widgets page. It extends the theme form rather than tracking its absence. Not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#514 ("More personalizable collections - Analysis", closed as completed) was the analysis for more personalizable SPA collections; it did not deliver the theme form. Background context. - IQSS/dataverse#12669 ("Uploading an Image resets the Dataverse Collection Theme form") is a bug in the legacy theme form. Unrelated to the SPA gap, but confirms the legacy form is the reference behavior. - No issue tracking the missing SPA theme form was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "theme", "theme widgets", "branding", "collection theme customization", "logo upload collection" and "tagline" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting "Theme + Widgets" for a collection opens a theme form in the SPA instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] The form supports inheriting the parent collection's theme - [ ] The form supports uploading and removing the logo, thumbnail and footer images, with the legacy type and size validation - [ ] Once a logo is present, the form offers the Logo Format choice (Square / Rectangle), and for Rectangle the Logo Alignment (Left / Center / Right) and Logo Background Color - [ ] Once a footer image is present, the form offers its alignment and background color - [ ] The form supports setting header background, link and text colors - [ ] The form supports setting a tagline (140 characters or fewer) and a website link - [ ] Saving persists the theme and it is reflected on the collection page; Cancel discards changes - [ ] The entry is only offered to users permitted to edit the collection - [ ] Covered by an automated test for saving and for inheriting a theme

jp.title: Site header missing superuser "Dashboard" entry; no dashboard route in the new frontend
jp.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF gives superusers a "Dashboard" entry in the site header's user dropdown, which opens the administrative dashboard (`/dashboard.xhtml`) — the single entry point for Harvesting Clients, Harvesting Server, Metadata Export, user management, and Move Dataset / Move Dataverse. The new frontend's user dropdown has no Dashboard entry for superusers, and no dashboard route exists, so none of the administrative dashboard is reachable from the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior The header's user dropdown renders a divider followed by a "Dashboard" link, but only when the logged-in user is a superuser (`rendered="#{dataverseSession.user.superuser}"`). The link points at `/dashboard.xhtml?dataverseId=` and opens a page of administrative cards. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as a superuser (`dataverseAdmin`). 2. Click the user name ("Dataverse Admin") in the top-right of the site header to open the dropdown. 3. Observe the "Dashboard" entry below the API Token entry, separated by dividers. 4. Click "Dashboard" and observe the dashboard page at `/dashboard.xhtml` with the Harvesting Clients, Harvesting Server, Metadata Export, Users, and Data cards. ## New frontend behavior The equivalent user dropdown in the modern frontend lists only My Data, Notifications, Account Information, API Token, and Log Out. There is no Dashboard entry, and no superuser-conditional entry of any kind — `LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx` contains no `user.superuser` branch. Navigating directly to a plausible dashboard URL redirects to the SPA's 404 page. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as the same superuser (`dataverseAdmin`). 2. Click "Dataverse Admin" in the header to open the user dropdown. 3. Observe that only My Data, Notifications, Account Information, API Token and Log Out are listed — no Dashboard entry appears, even though the user is a superuser. 4. Navigate directly to http://localhost:8000/modern/dashboard and observe the redirect to `/modern/404` ("WE CAN'T FIND THE PAGE YOU'RE LOOKING FOR"). ## Expected behavior A superuser signed into the new frontend should have a way to reach the administrative dashboard from the site header, matching the legacy placement in the user dropdown, and the entry should be hidden for non-superusers. ## Current behavior The feature is entirely absent from the SPA. No menu entry is rendered for superusers, no dashboard route is registered, and no "Not Implemented" placeholder is shown — there is nothing to click. A superuser must fall back to the legacy JSF UI to reach any dashboard function. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy header user dropdown for a superuser, showing the "Dashboard" entry between dividers, with the destination `/dashboard.xhtml` page and its administrative cards visible behind it. ### New frontend Modern frontend header user dropdown for the same superuser, listing only My Data, Notifications, Account Information, API Token and Log Out — the Dashboard entry is absent. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml) (superuser-gated `h:outputLink` to `/dashboard.xhtml`), [`src/main/webapp/dashboard.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dashboard.xhtml) (the dashboard cards), `header.dashboard` in `src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: no dashboard route or component found — [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) has no dashboard route, [`src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx) renders the user dropdown with no superuser branch, and no `dashboard` string exists under `public/locales/en/` - Missing-items entry: "Site Header - Go to Dashboard" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#258 ("admin dashboard: allow graphical creation of builtin users") requests a new capability on the dashboard's Manage Users page; it presupposes the dashboard exists rather than tracking its absence in the SPA. Not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#309 ("Add 'Move Dataverse collection' to the Move Data part of the Dashboard") and IQSS/dataverse-frontend#603 ("Allow forced move of dataverse datasets and collections from the Dataverse dashboard") are enhancements to individual dashboard cards, not the missing dashboard entry point. Not duplicates, but both depend on this. - IQSS/dataverse#11336 ("Dashboard - Users - Superuser (A-Z) & Superuser (Z-A) Sorting Swapped") is a bug in the legacy dashboard's user list. Unrelated to the SPA gap. - No issue tracking the absence of the dashboard (or its header entry) in the new frontend was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse, or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "dashboard", "admin dashboard", "superuser dashboard", "dashboard-users", "move dataset dashboard", "harvesting clients UI" and "header dashboard link" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A superuser signed into the new frontend sees a "Dashboard" entry in the header user dropdown, in the same position as legacy - [ ] The entry is not rendered for users who are not superusers - [ ] Selecting it navigates to a dashboard view in the SPA rather than 404ing or deep-linking into the JSF app - [ ] The dashboard view exposes the legacy dashboard's functions (Harvesting Clients, Harvesting Server, Metadata Export, Manage Users, Move Dataset, Move Dataverse), or links to them, with any not-yet-ported function clearly marked - [ ] Covered by an automated test asserting the entry appears for a superuser and is absent for a regular user

jp.title: Site-wide dismissible banner messages are not rendered in the new frontend
jp.body:
## Summary Admins can post a site-wide announcement banner (via the Banner Message admin API/feature) that logged-in users can dismiss for their session. The SPA doesn't render these admin-configured banners at all - only its own hardcoded "Modern version" notice is shown. ## Legacy JSF behavior An active banner message (created via POST /api/admin/bannerMessage) renders at the top of every page, with a clickable "x" that dismisses it for the session. ### Steps to observe 1. Create an active banner message via the API: POST http://localhost:8080/api/admin/bannerMessage with a JSON body containing "dismissibleByUser": "true" and a "messageTexts" array (e.g. [{"lang":"en","message":"
Test banner
"}]). 2. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) and navigate to any page. 3. Observe the banner rendered at the top of the page, with a clickable "x" dismiss control. ## New frontend behavior With the identical banner message active (same API state), nothing beyond the SPA's own static "You are using the new Dataverse Modern version" notice is shown. The admin-configured banner is not fetched/rendered at all, so there is also nothing to dismiss. ### Steps to reproduce 1. With the banner message from step 1 above still active, log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Navigate to any page (e.g. the root collection). 3. Observe that only the hardcoded "Modern version" notice appears; the admin-configured banner text is nowhere on the page. ## Expected behavior The SPA should fetch active banner messages (equivalent to GET /api/admin/bannerMessage or the public-facing equivalent) and display them, with a dismiss control that persists the dismissal for the user's session, matching legacy behavior. ## Current behavior Feature not implemented; admin-configured banner messages are invisible in the SPA regardless of whether they are marked dismissible. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy page showing the active banner message with its dismiss ("x") control at the top. ### New frontend Modern frontend showing only the static "Modern version" notice, with the same admin-configured banner message active but not rendered anywhere. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml (closeButton commandButton), src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseSession.java (dismissMessage(BannerMessage)), src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/api/Admin.java (addBannerMessage endpoint) - New frontend source: no equivalent banner-fetching/rendering component found - Missing-items entry: "Site Header - Dismiss Banner Message" in DV - Missing items.md ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#246 ("Add a banner on JSF to 'try the new UI' in the beta testing environment") discusses a different, hardcoded "try the new UI" banner concept for the legacy app - not the same as rendering admin-configured BannerMessage content in the SPA. Not a duplicate. - No duplicate found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse, or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc after searching "banner message" and related terms. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The SPA fetches active banner messages from the backend on page load - [ ] Active banner messages are rendered at the top of the page (or another consistent location) across all SPA pages - [ ] A dismiss control is shown for dismissible banners, and dismissal persists for the user's session - [ ] Behavior matches legacy for both dismissible and non-dismissible banner messages

iqss.title: Feature Complete: 403, 500 and other error pages
iqss.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF serves three distinct error pages, mapped by status code in `web.xml`: a 403 that tells the user they are not authorized and links them to installation support, a 500 that identifies an internal server error, and a 404. The new frontend differentiates only the 404 case; every other routing or loader failure renders one generic page reading "Oops, something went wrong..." with no status code, no indication of whether the problem is permissions or a server fault, and no support contact. ## Legacy JSF behavior `WEB-INF/web.xml` maps `403 -> /403.xhtml`, `500 -> /500.xhtml` and `404 -> /404static.xhtml`. - **403** renders "**Not Authorized** - You are not authorized to view this page. If you believe this is an error, please contact Support for assistance.", where the support name is a mailto/contact link. - **500** renders "**Internal Server Error** - An unexpected error was encountered, no more information is available." ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080). 2. Navigate to http://localhost:8080/403.xhtml and observe the Not Authorized message with its support contact link. 3. Navigate to http://localhost:8080/500.xhtml and observe the Internal Server Error message. ## New frontend behavior The SPA has exactly one differentiated error page — `NotFoundPage` at `/404` (`Route.NOT_FOUND_PAGE`), which correctly reports "We can't find the ... you're looking for." Everything else is handled by a single `errorElement`: `ErrorPage` is attached to the root route and to each child route in `src/router/routes.tsx`, and it renders only the strings from `public/locales/en/errorPage.json`: ```json { "message": { "heading": "Oops,", "errorText": "something went wrong..." }, "brandName": "Dataverse", "backToHomepage": "Back to {{brandName}} Homepage" } ``` There is no 403 route, no 500 route, and `ErrorPage` does not read the status from the route error — it ignores `useRouteError()`'s status entirely except for logging. So a permission failure and a server fault are visually indistinguishable to the user, and neither offers a support contact. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Navigate to any unknown path, for example http://localhost:8000/modern/dashboard/move-dataset, and observe that a 404 *is* handled (redirect to `/modern/404`). 3. Inspect `src/sections/Route.enum.ts` and confirm the only error route is `NOT_FOUND_PAGE = '/404'` — there is no 403 or 500 equivalent. 4. Inspect `src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx` and `public/locales/en/errorPage.json` and confirm the generic page carries no status code and no support link. ## Expected behavior A permission failure in the new frontend should render a 403-equivalent page that says the user is not authorized and points them at installation support, and an unexpected server error should render a 500-equivalent page that identifies it as a server error — rather than both collapsing into "Oops, something went wrong...". ## Current behavior Divergent, not entirely absent: the SPA handles 404 properly but has no 403 or 500 variants. Both conditions fall through to one generic error page that omits the status code, the permission-versus-server distinction, and the support contact that legacy provides on 403. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy 403 page: names the authorization problem and links to installation support. Legacy 500 page: identifies the failure as an internal server error. ### New frontend The SPA's only status-specific error page is the 404 shown below. **This is not the 403/500 path** — it is included to show that error pages exist but only for the not-found case. The generic `ErrorPage` that a 403 or 500 would produce could not be triggered on demand in a dev build, so its content is quoted above directly from `ErrorPage.tsx` and `errorPage.json` rather than screenshotted. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml) (`error-page` mappings), [`src/main/webapp/403.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/403.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/500.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/500.xhtml) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx) (generic, status-agnostic), [`src/router/routes.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/router/routes.tsx) (`errorElement: ` on every route), [`src/sections/not-found-page/NotFoundPage.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-found-page/NotFoundPage.tsx), `public/locales/en/errorPage.json` - Missing-items entries: "Error Pages - 403 Forbidden Page" and "Error Pages - 500 Internal Server Error Page" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - The sibling row "Error Pages - 404 Static Fallback Page" is **not** a gap: the SPA's `NotFoundPage` covers it. The only residual difference is that legacy's `404static.xhtml` is served by the application server while the SPA's 404 is a client-side route needing the JS bundle. - No issue covering SPA 403 or 500 error pages was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "403", "500", "error page", "forbidden" and "internal server error" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A permission failure renders a 403-equivalent page stating the user is not authorized - [ ] The 403 page offers a way to contact installation support, as legacy does - [ ] An unexpected server error renders a 500-equivalent page identifying it as a server error - [ ] The generic fallback distinguishes these cases rather than showing the same text for all failures - [ ] The existing 404 behavior is unchanged - [ ] Covered by automated tests asserting the 403 and 500 states render their respective pages ## Notes I am not sure if these are all the codes that need to be handled or if the SPA has another mechanism of escape for these other error codes.

iqss.title: superuser "Dashboard"
iqss.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF gives superusers a "Dashboard" entry in the site header's user dropdown, which opens the administrative dashboard (`/dashboard.xhtml`) — the single entry point for Harvesting Clients, Harvesting Server, Metadata Export, user management, and Move Dataset / Move Dataverse. Click "Dashboard" and observe the dashboard page at `/dashboard.xhtml` with the Harvesting Clients, Harvesting Server, Metadata Export, Users, and Data cards. ## New frontend behavior The equivalent user dropdown in the modern frontend lists only My Data, Notifications, Account Information, API Token, and Log Out. There is no Dashboard entry, and no superuser-conditional entry of any kind — `LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx` contains no `user.superuser` branch. Navigating directly to a plausible dashboard URL redirects to the SPA's 404 page. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Navigate directly to http://localhost:8000/modern/dashboard and observe the redirect to `/modern/404` ("WE CAN'T FIND THE PAGE YOU'RE LOOKING FOR"). ## Expected behavior A superuser signed into the new frontend should have a way to reach the administrative dashboard from the site header, matching the legacy placement in the user dropdown, and the entry should be hidden for non-superusers. ## Current behavior The feature is entirely absent from the SPA. No menu entry is rendered for superusers, no dashboard route is registered, and no "Not Implemented" placeholder is shown — there is nothing to click. A superuser must fall back to the legacy JSF UI to reach any dashboard function. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy header user dropdown for a superuser, showing the "Dashboard" entry between dividers, with the destination `/dashboard.xhtml` page and its administrative cards visible behind it. ### New frontend Modern frontend header user dropdown for the same superuser, listing only My Data, Notifications, Account Information, API Token and Log Out — the Dashboard entry is absent. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml) (superuser-gated `h:outputLink` to `/dashboard.xhtml`), [`src/main/webapp/dashboard.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dashboard.xhtml) (the dashboard cards), `header.dashboard` in `src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: no dashboard route or component found — [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) has no dashboard route, [`src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx) renders the user dropdown with no superuser branch, and no `dashboard` string exists under `public/locales/en/` - Missing-items entry: "Site Header - Go to Dashboard" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#258 ("admin dashboard: allow graphical creation of builtin users") requests a new capability on the dashboard's Manage Users page; it presupposes the dashboard exists rather than tracking its absence in the SPA. iqss.title: Feature Complete: Downloads metrics panel

Observe the "Metrics | 0 Downloads" panel above the collection description. ## New frontend behavior The SPA collection page renders the breadcrumb, title, description, Contact / Share actions, the search box and the items panel — but no metrics panel. There is no collection-level metrics component: `src/sections/collection/` contains no metrics module, and the only metrics code, `src/sections/homepage/metrics/Metrics.tsx`, is homepage-only and sourced from `useGetInstallationMetrics` via `dataverseHubRepository` (Dataverse Hub aggregate data, which is why a fresh local install displays figures like 304K datasets and 170M downloads). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Navigate to the root collection at `/modern/collections/root`. 3. Observe that no metrics or download count appears anywhere on the page — only Contact and Share beside the title. ## Expected behavior The collection page in the new frontend should show that collection's usage metrics — at minimum the download count legacy shows — sourced from the installation's own metrics for that collection rather than from aggregate Hub data. ## Current behavior Absent. No collection-level metrics panel exists in the SPA. The homepage metrics block is unrelated: it reports cross-installation Dataverse Hub aggregates, not this collection's usage. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy root collection page: the "Metrics | 0 Downloads" panel is visible above the description, beside Contact / Share / Edit. ### New frontend Modern frontend root collection page, same collection and window size: only Contact and Share — no metrics panel and no download count. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse.xhtml) (collection metrics panel), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseServiceBean.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseServiceBean.java), `/api/info/metrics/downloads` family - New frontend source: no collection metrics component found under [`src/sections/collection/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/collection); the only metrics code is [`src/sections/homepage/metrics/Metrics.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/homepage/metrics/Metrics.tsx) with `useGetInstallationMetrics` / `dataverseHubRepository`, which is homepage-scoped and Hub-sourced - Missing-items entry: "Dataverse Page - View Root Dataverse Download Metrics" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#474 ("Feature Request/Idea: Dataverse metrics bar at sub-dataverse level") asks to extend usage metrics to sub-collections, and explicitly notes that Dataverse "already provides download and Make Data Count metrics in the GUI at the installation/top-level collection level". It presupposes the top-level collection metrics this issue reports as missing from the SPA, so it depends on this rather than duplicating it. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#779 ("Show MDC metrics in SPA Dataset page") is the dataset-level counterpart. Same theme, different object; not a duplicate. - No issue reporting the absent collection-level metrics panel in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "collection metrics downloads", "dataverse metrics panel SPA", "collection downloads count" and "installation metrics homepage" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The collection page in the new frontend shows that collection's download count - [ ] The figure reflects the installation's own metrics for that collection, not Dataverse Hub aggregates - [ ] It is visible to anonymous visitors, as in legacy - [ ] It renders sensibly at zero ("0 Downloads") and while loading - [ ] Covered by an automated test asserting the collection metric renders ## Notes - This still need to be configured [:MetricsUrl](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/6.12.1/installation/config.html#id534) - The data currently displayed on the JSF version is an accurate number, this will change due the API being changed and report the same number than the API.

iqss.title: Feature Complete: Dataset Private/Preview URL creation opens placeholder in the new frontend
iqss.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a dataset editor create a shareable review link for an unpublished draft — called "Preview URL" in 6.11 (formerly "Private URL") — then copy it or disable it, with an anonymized variant when the installation configures anonymized fields. In the new frontend the dataset Edit menu still lists "Private URL", but the entry is wired to the shared not-implemented handler, so no review link can be created, copied or disabled. ## Legacy JSF behavior Edit Dataset -> "Preview URL" opens the "Unpublished Dataset Preview URL" dialog. For a draft it offers **Create General Preview URL**; once created it shows the generated `previewurl.xhtml?token=...` link with **Copy to Clipboard** and **Disable General Preview URL**. For a published version it refuses with "Preview URL can only be used with unpublished versions of datasets." Only one Preview URL can be active per draft. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open an **unpublished draft** dataset (this review used `doi:10.5072/FK2/8PW3WO`). 3. Open the "Edit Dataset" dropdown and select "Preview URL". 4. Click "Create General Preview URL" and observe the generated link with "Copy to Clipboard" and "Disable General Preview URL". ## New frontend behavior `EditDatasetMenu.tsx` lists the entry as `EditDatasetMenuItems.PRIVATE_URL`, shown when the user can manage dataset or file permissions, and its handler is: ```tsx if (eventKey === EditDatasetMenuItems.PRIVATE_URL) { showModal() return } ``` So it opens the "Not Implemented" modal. The SPA *can consume* a preview URL token (`getDatasetByPrivateUrlToken`, anonymized view in `DatasetFactory.tsx`), but it provides no way to create, copy or disable one. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open an unpublished draft dataset you can edit and open the "Edit Dataset" dropdown. 3. Select "Private URL". 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal. No link is created and none can be copied or disabled. ## Expected behavior A user who can manage dataset permissions should be able to create a preview/private URL for a draft from the new frontend, copy it, and disable it — plus create the anonymized variant where the installation enables it — and be told clearly that the feature applies only to unpublished versions. ## Current behavior The menu entry is present but non-functional — it opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Creating a review link requires leaving the SPA for the legacy JSF page, even though the SPA already understands the resulting token. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Unpublished Dataset Preview URL" dialog on a draft dataset after creating the link: the generated `previewurl.xhtml?token=...` URL with "Copy to Clipboard" and "Disable General Preview URL". **Scope note:** only the "General Preview" option appeared. The anonymized variant depends on `:AnonymizedFieldTypeNames`, which is not set in this install, so the anonymized flow could not be exercised and is described from source. ### New frontend The shared "Not Implemented" modal that this entry opens. **Note:** this capture was taken from the *collection* Edit dropdown, which uses the same `NotImplementedModal` component that `EditDatasetMenu`'s `showModal()` triggers. iqss.title: Feature Complete: Dataset and file permissions management
iqss.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a dataset curator manage who can access a dataset and its restricted files: assign and remove roles on the dataset, and — on a separate file-permissions screen — grant or reject file access requests (individually or in bulk), revoke granted access, and review the request history. In the new frontend the dataset Edit menu still shows a "Permissions" submenu with "Dataset" and "File" entries, but both are wired to the shared not-implemented handler, so neither screen is reachable. ## Legacy JSF behavior Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> **Dataset** opens `permissions-manage.xhtml`, which lists the users and groups with access, their roles, an "Assign Roles to Users/Groups" action and a "Remove Assigned Role" action per row, plus a Roles panel. Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> **File** opens `permissions-manage-files.xhtml`, which lists restricted files and pending access requests with: Grant Access, Grant All / Grant Selected, Reject All / Reject Selected, Revoke access for an already-granted user, toggles to show deleted files and the access-request history, and a download of the file-permissions history. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a dataset, then Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> Dataset (or `/permissions-manage.xhtml?id=`). 3. Observe the Users/Groups table with "Assign Roles to Users/Groups" and "Remove Assigned Role". 4. Choose Permissions -> File (`/permissions-manage-files.xhtml?id=`) and observe the file-access request and grant controls. ## New frontend behavior `EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx` renders the submenu and attaches the not-implemented handler to the whole dropdown: ```tsx {dataset.permissions.canManageDatasetPermissions && ( {t('...permissions.dataset')})} {dataset.permissions.canManageFilesPermissions && ( {t('...permissions.file')})} ``` So selecting either "Dataset" or "File" opens the "Not Implemented" modal. There is no dataset-permissions or file-permissions route or component in the SPA. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a dataset you can administer and open the "Edit Dataset" dropdown. 3. Open the "Permissions" submenu and select "Dataset" (then repeat for "File"). 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal in both cases. ## Expected behavior A dataset curator should be able to manage dataset role assignments in the new frontend (list, assign, remove) and handle file access requests (grant or reject individually and in bulk, revoke granted access, review and export the request history, and optionally show deleted files) — gated on `canManageDatasetPermissions` and `canManageFilesPermissions` respectively. ## Current behavior Both submenu entries are present but non-functional — they open the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Dataset access administration requires leaving the SPA for the legacy JSF pages. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy dataset Permissions page for a draft test dataset: Users/Groups with their roles, "Assign Roles to Users/Groups", and "Remove Assigned Role" per assignment. **Scope note:** the *file* permissions screen could not be shown with meaningful content. It lists restricted files and access requests, and no data file can exist in this install — its only storage driver is `s3`, pointed at AWS with placeholder credentials and no S3 service running, so every upload fails. The file-side controls are therefore described from `permissions-manage-files.xhtml` rather than screenshotted. ### New frontend The shared "Not Implemented" modal that both entries open. **Note:** this capture was taken from the *collection* Edit dropdown, which uses the same `NotImplementedModal` component that `EditDatasetPermissionsMenu`'s `showModal` triggers. The SPA session expired partway through this review and re-authenticating requires a password, so a capture from the dataset Permissions submenu specifically is pending; the wiring is quoted above. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/permissions-manage.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/permissions-manage.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/permissions-manage-files.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/permissions-manage-files.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/roles-assign.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/roles-assign.xhtml) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx) (`onSelect={showModal}`); no permissions route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Manage Dataset Permissions", "Dataset Page - Manage File Permissions" and the nine "Manage File Permissions" rows in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#2 (collection "Manage Permissions" opens placeholder) is the collection-level counterpart, stubbed the same way. Same pattern, different object. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#19 (Private/Preview URL creation) and #18 (Thumbnails + Widgets) are sibling entries in the same dataset Edit menu. - IQSS/dataverse#12076 ("Dataverse linking still requires superuser despite introduction of LinkDataverse permission") concerns permission semantics rather than this UI. Not a duplicate. - No issue covering SPA dataset or file permission management was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "dataset permissions SPA", "file access requests", "grant file access" and "manage permissions" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Permissions -> Dataset opens a role-assignment view instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] Roles can be assigned to users and groups, and existing assignments removed - [ ] Permissions -> File opens a file-access view listing restricted files and pending requests - [ ] Access requests can be granted and rejected individually and in bulk - [ ] Granted access can be revoked - [ ] The access-request history can be reviewed and exported, and deleted files optionally shown - [ ] The two entries respect `canManageDatasetPermissions` and `canManageFilesPermissions` - [ ] Covered by automated tests for assigning a role and for granting and rejecting a file access request

iqss.title: Feature Complete: Account Information is read-only in the new frontend: no edit, password change or email verification
iqss.body:
## Summary Legacy JSF lets a user manage their own account: edit their name, email, affiliation and position, change their password, and re-send the email-verification message when their address is unverified. The new frontend's Account Information tab is a **read-only table** — it displays the same fields but offers no edit, no password change and no email verification. The SPA source marks all three as TODO. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dataverseuser.xhtml` (Account Information tab) shows Username, Given Name, Family Name, Email, Affiliation and Position, with an "Edit Account" dropdown offering **Edit Account Information** and **Change Password**. An unverified address is flagged "Not Verified" beside a **Send Verification Email** button. The edit form saves or cancels. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Go to Account -> Account Information (`/dataverseuser.xhtml?selectTab=accountInfo`). 3. Observe the "Edit Account" dropdown and, next to the email, the "Not Verified" flag with "Send Verification Email". 4. Choose Edit Account Information, change a field and save or cancel; choose Change Password and set a new one. ## New frontend behavior `AccountInfoSection.tsx` renders a plain table of the session user's fields and nothing else. Its first lines are the SPA authors' own TODOs: ```tsx // TODO - Add verified email icon // TODO - Edit account information // TODO - Change password export const AccountInfoSection = () => { const { user } = useSession() return ({/* username, givenName, familyName, email, affiliation, position */}
) } ``` `public/locales/en/account.json` correspondingly has keys only for the field labels under `info.*` — there are no strings for editing, saving, cancelling, password change or email verification. The Notifications section likewise has no muting controls (no `mute` reference anywhere in `src/sections/account/notifications-section/`). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Open the user menu and choose "Account Information". 3. Observe the fields rendered as static text, with no Edit, Change Password or email-verification control anywhere on the tab. ## Expected behavior A user should be able to edit their own account details, change their password, and trigger email verification from the new frontend, with the unverified state visibly flagged — matching the legacy Account Information tab. ## Current behavior Read-only. The SPA shows account details but provides no way to change them; password changes and email verification must be done in the legacy JSF UI (or, for OIDC-backed accounts, in the identity provider). ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy Account Information tab: the "Edit Account" dropdown (Edit Account Information / Change Password) and the email flagged "Not Verified" with a "Send Verification Email" button. ### New frontend ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseUserPage.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseUserPage.java) (edit account, change password, `sendVerificationEmail`) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/account/account-info-section/AccountInfoSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/account-info-section/AccountInfoSection.tsx) (read-only, with the TODOs quoted above), `public/locales/en/account.json` (`info.*` labels only), [`src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx) (no muting) - Missing-items entries: "Account Information" rows (Edit Account Information, Save Account Changes, Change Password, Save New Password, Cancel Edit, Verify Email Address) in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#712 ("SPA User Menu Navigation Breaks After Visiting Account Information", closed) touched this same tab but concerned navigation, not editing. Not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1020 ("Redesign the Dataverse account creation workflow to encourage users to add ORCIDs") and #1022 ("Let a user add a ROR to describe their affiliation during account creation") both propose changes to account *creation*; they assume account details are editable. Related, not duplicates. - For OIDC-backed installations, password change belongs to the identity provider (see IQSS/dataverse-frontend#652, closed, which established that the SPA delegates login to a themed Keycloak page). Scoping this issue should decide whether "Change Password" is in scope for the SPA at all, or whether it should link out to the provider. - No issue covering editable account information in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "edit account information SPA", "change password SPA", "account information" and "verify email SPA" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A user can edit their given name, family name, email, affiliation and position from the Account Information tab - [ ] Changes are saved, and Cancel discards them without saving - [ ] An unverified email address is visibly flagged and a verification email can be re-sent - [ ] A password change is offered for builtin accounts, or the tab links to the identity provider where that is the correct owner — whichever the maintainers decide, the current silent absence is resolved - [ ] Covered by automated tests for editing and saving account details

iqss.title: Feature Complete: Curation status
iqss.body: ## Summary This installation configures curation labels, and the new frontend correctly renders them: the dataset "Publish Dataset" menu shows a "Change Curation Status" submenu listing Author Contacted, Privacy Review, Awaiting Paper Publication, Final Approval and "Remove Current Status". Selecting any of them opens the "Not Implemented" modal instead of applying the status, so a curator cannot set, change or clear a dataset's curation status from the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior With curation labels configured, a curator can set a draft dataset's curation status from the dataset page, change it to another allowed label, or remove it. Legacy reports the outcome ("Curation Status Changed", "Curation Status is now \"{0}\"", "Curation Status Removed") and rejects invalid attempts with specific messages — label not allowed, status unchanged, labeling disabled, or the version already released (status can only be set on drafts). ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a **draft** dataset. 3. Set a curation status from the allowed labels, confirm the "Curation Status is now ..." confirmation, then remove it again. ## New frontend behavior `ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx` reads the allowed labels from the `ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_STATUSES` setting and renders one item per label plus "Remove Current Status" — but every item is wired to the same handler: ```tsx const handleItemClick = (event: React.MouseEvent) => { event.stopPropagation() showModal() // useNotImplementedModal } ``` So the submenu is fully populated and looks functional, but each selection opens the "Not Implemented" modal. There is no curation-status history view either. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a draft dataset — this review used `doi:10.5072/FK2/Q9LZAD`. 3. Open the "Publish Dataset" dropdown and hover/open "Change Curation Status". 4. Select any label, for example "Privacy Review". 5. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal; the dataset's curation status is unchanged. ## Expected behavior A curator should be able to set a draft dataset's curation status to any allowed label, change it, and remove it from the new frontend, with the resulting status visible on the dataset and the legacy rejection cases handled (label not allowed, no change, labeling disabled, version already released). The status history should also be viewable, as legacy records it. ## Current behavior The submenu is present and correctly populated from configuration, which makes it look implemented, but every option opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Nothing is applied and no history is shown. This is more misleading than an absent control, because the labels render correctly. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Not screenshotted: setting a curation status changes real dataset state, and the legacy flow was left untouched deliberately. The behavior is established from the `dataset.curationstatus.*` bundle keys (`header`="Curation Status Changed", `info`="Curation Status is now \"{0}\"", `removed`="Curation Status Removed", plus the four failure cases) and from the fact that this installation's labels are configured — the SPA reads and displays them, as the screenshots below show. ### New frontend The populated "Change Curation Status" submenu on a draft dataset: Author Contacted, Privacy Review, Awaiting Paper Publication, Final Approval, and Remove Current Status. Selecting "Privacy Review" opens the "Not Implemented" modal, with the submenu still visible behind it. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: `dataset.curationstatus.*` keys in [`Bundle.properties`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties); API: `/api/datasets/$id/curationStatus` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx) (every item calls `showModal()`), [`src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Change Curation Status", "Remove Curation Status" and "View Curation Status History" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#18, #19 and #20 are the other dataset-level controls stubbed with the same `NotImplementedModal`. Same pattern, different features. - The sibling "Submit for Review" control is stubbed the same way (`SubmitForReviewButton.tsx` has `onClick={showModal}`), but it only renders for a user who can update and **not** publish a dataset, so it could not be exercised with the single superuser account available here. Worth folding into the same work. - No issue covering curation-status management in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "curation status", "external status", "curation label" and "submit for review" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting a curation label applies it to the draft dataset instead of opening the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] The applied status is visible on the dataset - [ ] "Remove Current Status" clears it - [ ] Rejections are surfaced clearly: label not allowed, status unchanged, labeling disabled, and version already released - [ ] Curation status history can be viewed - [ ] The submenu only appears for users permitted to curate, and only for draft versions - [ ] Covered by automated tests for setting and removing a status

iqss.title: Feature Complete: Publish Collection confirmation dialog bug.
iqss.body: # Publishing a sub-collection with an unpublished parent shows a Continue/Cancel confirmation instead of legacy's blocked-publish notice ## Summary When a user publishes a collection whose parent collection is unpublished, legacy JSF blocks the action and explains why. The new frontend shows its normal publish confirmation with **Continue** and **Cancel**, as if publishing could succeed. This is a behavior mismatch, not just a missing warning. The SPA should block the action as legacy does, rather than add a warning to a confirmation that cannot succeed. ## Legacy JSF behavior | Key | Legacy string | |---|---| | `dataverse.publish.failed` | "Cannot publish dataverse." | | `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` | "This dataverse cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published." | ### Steps to observe 1. Create an unpublished collection `A` under a published collection (for example, root). 2. Create a collection `B` inside `A`, and leave both unpublished. 3. Open `B` in the JSF UI and click **Publish**. 4. A dialog titled "Cannot publish dataverse." explains that the parent has not been published. It offers no option to continue publishing. ## New frontend behavior The SPA opens the generic publish modal on `/spa/collections/`: "Are you sure you want to publish your collection? Once you do so it must remain published." The modal has **Continue** and **Cancel** buttons. Nothing tells the user that the parent is unpublished. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use the same setup as above: collection `B` inside unpublished collection `A`. 2. Open `B` in the new frontend and click **Publish**. 3. The generic Continue/Cancel confirmation appears. 4. Click **Continue**. Result: [Needed: confirm whether the API error is shown, swallowed, or shown as a generic failure toast] ## Expected behavior - The SPA checks whether the parent collection is published before it shows the publish confirmation. - If the parent is unpublished, the SPA shows a blocking notice equivalent to `dataverse.publish.failed` / `dataverse.publish.failed.tip`, with only a close/OK action. - The SPA offers no **Continue** action and sends no publish request. - Collections with a published parent keep the current confirmation flow unchanged. ## Current behavior The SPA always shows the Continue/Cancel confirmation, whether or not the parent is published. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF ### New frontend ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF strings: `Bundle.properties`, https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties (`dataverse.publish.failed`, `dataverse.publish.failed.tip`) - New frontend collection publish: `src/sections/collection/publish-collection/`, https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/collection/publish-collection - New frontend use case: `src/collection/domain/useCases/publishCollection.ts` - Inventory entry: "Dataverse Page - Blocked Publish Notice" in `DV - Missing items.md` / `data/jsf-feature-inventory-MODEL 1.tsv:14` ## Related issues - #23: Publish-blocked warnings are incomplete. Closed, and moved to IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1121. It covers this case, but describes it as a missing *warning before confirmation*, not as the action being *blocked*. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1121: Feature Complete: Publish warning is incomplete. Its expected behavior allows "offering to publish the chain", which legacy does not do for collections. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#461 / PR #500: Publish Collection. Introduced the current Continue/Cancel modal. Its spec did not consider an unpublished parent. - No other issue covering this behavior was found in jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc or IQSS/dataverse-frontend (open or closed). ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished shows a blocking notice that matches legacy's `dataverse.publish.failed` / `.tip` message. - [ ] That notice offers no Continue/publish action, and no publish API request is sent. - [ ] Publishing a collection whose parent is published keeps the existing Continue/Cancel confirmation. - [ ] Automated tests cover both the unpublished-parent and published-parent cases.

iqss.title: Feature Complete: Publish warning is incomplete
iqss.body: ## Summary The new frontend handles the simple publish-blocked case correctly — a dataset whose immediate parent collection is unpublished gets legacy's exact "Would you like to publish both right now?" prompt. But it misses the other two cases legacy distinguishes: when **two generations** of ancestors are unpublished it still offers to publish "both", naming only the immediate parent; and when **a collection** whose parent is unpublished is published, the SPA shows a generic confirmation with no warning at all. ## Legacy JSF behavior Legacy has three distinct messages: | Case | Legacy string | | --- | --- | | Dataset, parent unpublished, user can publish it | `dataset.mayNotPublish.both`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} is published. Would you like to publish both right now?" | | Dataset, **two** generations unpublished | `dataset.mayNotPublish.twoGenerations`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} **and {1}** are published." | | Dataset, parent must be published by someone else | `dataset.mayNotPublish.administrator`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} is published by its administrator." | And for collections: `dataverse.publish.failed` ("Cannot publish dataverse.") with `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` — "This dataverse cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published." ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Create an unpublished collection inside another unpublished collection, and a dataset inside the inner one. 3. Attempt to publish that dataset and observe the two-generations message naming both ancestors. 4. Attempt to publish the inner collection and observe the "cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published" notice. ## New frontend behavior **Two generations (dataset).** With `Root > QA Test Collection (unpublished) > Gap Review Subcollection 184 (unpublished) > dataset`, the SPA's Publish Dataset modal says only "This dataset cannot be published until **Gap Review Subcollection 184** is published. Would you like to publish both right now?" — the `.both` variant. It names one ancestor and offers to publish "both", although two ancestors are unpublished, so accepting cannot succeed as described. **Collection.** Publishing `Gap Review Subcollection 184`, whose parent `QA Test Collection` is unpublished, opens a Publish Collection modal reading only "Are you sure you want to publish your collection? Once you do so it must remain published." — no mention that the parent is unpublished and no equivalent of legacy's blocked-publish notice. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open the dataset at `/modern/datasets?persistentId=doi:10.5072/FK2/SSQN4W&version=DRAFT` (inside two unpublished collections). 3. Publish Dataset -> Publish, and observe the single-ancestor "publish both" wording. 4. Open `/modern/collections/gap-review-sub-184` and click Publish; observe the generic confirmation with no unpublished-parent warning. ## Expected behavior - A dataset with more than one unpublished ancestor should say so and name them, rather than offering to publish "both". - A dataset whose parent can only be published by someone else should say that, as legacy's `administrator` variant does. - Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished should warn, and either offer to publish the chain or explain why it cannot proceed — not present a plain confirmation. ## Current behavior Only the single-parent dataset case is handled. The other cases either show misleading wording (two generations) or no warning at all (collection), so a user can confirm an action whose stated effect is wrong. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Not screenshotted: reproducing these states in legacy means publishing collections, which permanently changes install data, and the legacy flow was deliberately left untouched. The three dataset variants and the collection notice are quoted verbatim from `Bundle.properties` above. ### New frontend Two unpublished generations (`Root > QA Test Collection > Gap Review Subcollection 184 > dataset`), yet the modal names only the immediate parent and offers to publish "both": Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished — a generic confirmation with no warning: ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: `dataset.mayNotPublish.both`, `dataset.mayNotPublish.twoGenerations`, `dataset.mayNotPublish.administrator`, `dataverse.publish.failed` and `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` in [`Bundle.properties`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/publish-dataset/PublishDatasetModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/publish-dataset/PublishDatasetModal.tsx) and [`PublishDatasetMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/PublishDatasetMenu.tsx); the collection side in [`src/sections/collection/publish-collection/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/collection/publish-collection) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Publish Blocked - Two Generations Unpublished" and "Dataverse Page - Blocked Publish Notice" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - The sibling row "Dataset Page - Publish Blocked - Parent Unpublished" is **not** a gap: the SPA reproduces legacy's `.both` message word for word. Only the two-generations and collection variants are missing. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#22 (curation status stubs) is the other finding from the same dataset publish menu. - No issue covering these publish-blocked variants was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "publish blocked", "cannot be published", "publish both" and "unpublished parent" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A dataset with two or more unpublished ancestors reports all of them and does not offer a "publish both" action that cannot succeed - [ ] A dataset whose ancestor must be published by another user gets the administrator variant of the message - [ ] Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished warns before the confirmation, matching legacy's blocked-publish notice - [ ] The existing single-parent dataset case keeps its current wording and behavior - [ ] Covered by automated tests for the two-generations and collection cases
