iqss.title: Feature Complete: Notification settings pannel
iqss.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF can let users choose which notifications they receive, separately for email and in-app delivery, from a "Notification settings" panel on the Notifications tab. **This panel is opt-in per installation: it only appears when an admin enables the `:ShowMuteOptions` database setting, which is `false` by default.** The new frontend's Notifications tab lists and dismisses notifications but has no muting controls, so on an installation that has turned muting on, users of the new frontend can't opt out of any notification type, including the emails. > [!IMPORTANT] > **You won't see this feature on a default installation.** The legacy panel is hidden unless `:ShowMuteOptions` is set to `true`. See [Enabling the feature](#enabling-the-feature-legacy-jsf) below before trying to reproduce. ## Enabling the feature (legacy JSF) Notification muting is controlled by three installation-wide **database settings**. They're stored in the `setting` table, have no admin UI, and are managed through the admin settings API (usually only reachable from localhost or with the API unblock key): | Setting | Default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `:ShowMuteOptions` | `false` | When `true`, shows the "Notification settings" panel on the Notifications tab. When unset or `false`, the panel is not rendered at all. | | `:AlwaysMuted` | empty | Comma-separated notification types (e.g. `ASSIGNROLE,REVOKEROLE`) that are always muted. Users can't turn them on. | | `:NeverMuted` | empty | Comma-separated notification types that are never muted. Users can't turn them off. | Types listed in `:AlwaysMuted` or `:NeverMuted` show in the panel as greyed-out (disabled) checkboxes. If a type appears in both, `:AlwaysMuted` wins and a warning is logged. These settings were added in Dataverse 5.11. ```bash # Enable the panel curl -X PUT -d true http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions # Optional: lock some types so they show as disabled checkboxes curl -X PUT -d 'ASSIGNROLE,REVOKEROLE' http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:AlwaysMuted curl -X PUT -d 'CREATEACC' http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:NeverMuted # Check the current value curl http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions # Revert to default (panel hidden) curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions ``` Docs: Installation Guide → [`:ShowMuteOptions`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#showmuteoptions), [`:AlwaysMuted`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#alwaysmuted), [`:NeverMuted`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#nevermuted). User Guide → [Notifications](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/user/account.html#notifications). ## Legacy JSF behavior With `:ShowMuteOptions=true`, `dataverseuser.xhtml` renders a collapsible "Notification settings" panel above the notification list. It has two multi-select checkbox groups and a "Save Changes" button: - `notification.mutedEmails`: "Select the email notifications you wish to receive:" - `notification.mutedNotifications`: "Select the in-app notifications you wish to receive:" Unchecking a type mutes that notification for that delivery channel. Users can also manage the same preferences through the API: `GET /api/notifications/mutedEmails`, `PUT`/`DELETE /api/notifications/mutedEmails/{typeName}`, and the same endpoints for `mutedNotifications`. ### Steps to observe 1. Enable the setting as a superuser: `curl -X PUT -d true http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions` (see [Enabling the feature](#enabling-the-feature-legacy-jsf)). 2. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 3. Go to Account → Notifications (`/dataverseuser.xhtml?selectTab=notifications`). 4. Expand "Notification settings". 5. You should see the two checkbox groups for email and in-app notification types. Uncheck one and click "Save Changes" to mute it. ## New frontend behavior The SPA Notifications tab (`/modern/account?tab=notifications`) shows "Displaying 1 - N of N Notifications", each row with a dismiss (X) control, plus a "Clear All Notifications" action. There is no settings panel and no muting UI, whatever the value of `:ShowMuteOptions`. A case-insensitive search for `mute` across `src/sections/account/notifications-section/` and `public/locales/en/account.json` finds nothing. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Enable `:ShowMuteOptions` on the backend as above. 2. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 3. Open the user menu and choose "Notifications" (or go to `/modern/account?tab=notifications`). 4. You'll see the notification list with dismiss and "Clear All Notifications", and no notification-settings or muting control anywhere on the tab. ## Expected behavior When the installation has `:ShowMuteOptions=true`, users should be able to choose, per notification type, whether they get it by email and whether it appears in-app, the same way legacy's two checkbox groups work. The choice should be saved to their account. Types locked by `:AlwaysMuted` / `:NeverMuted` should be shown but not editable. When `:ShowMuteOptions` is false (the default), no muting UI should be shown, which matches legacy. ## Current behavior The SPA has no muting. On an installation with muting enabled, users can only dismiss notifications after they arrive. They can't stop unwanted notification emails without going back to the legacy JSF page or using the API. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF ### New frontend SPA Notifications tab: list with per-row dismiss and "Clear All Notifications", no notification-settings or muting panel. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: - [`src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml` L65–100](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml#L65-L100): the panel, gated by `jsf:rendered="#{settingsWrapper.showMuteOptions}"` - [`SettingsWrapper.java` L260–262](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/SettingsWrapper.java#L260-L262): `isShowMuteOptions()` defaults to `false`; also `isAlwaysMuted` / `isNeverMuted` - [`SettingsServiceBean.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/settings/SettingsServiceBean.java): `ShowMuteOptions`, `AlwaysMuted`, `NeverMuted` keys - [`DataverseUserPage.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/authorization/providers/builtin/DataverseUserPage.java): `toReceiveEmails`, `toReceiveNotifications`, `isDisabled` - API: [`api/Notifications.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/api/Notifications.java): `/api/notifications/mutedEmails[/{typeName}]` and `/api/notifications/mutedNotifications[/{typeName}]` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx) and [`NotificationsHelper.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsHelper.tsx): no muting, and no `mute` strings in `public/locales/en/account.json` - Missing-items entries: "Notifications - Manage Muted Email Notifications" and "Notifications - Manage Muted In-App Notifications" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#21 (Account Information is read-only) is the related gap in the same account area. Both are about account self-service that the SPA shows but doesn't let the user change. - No issue covering notification muting in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc. Searched "muted notifications", "notification settings", "mute" and "notification preferences" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The notification settings UI is shown only when `:ShowMuteOptions` is `true` and is hidden by default - [ ] The Notifications tab offers per-type control over which notifications the user receives by email - [ ] It offers the same control for in-app notifications, separately from email - [ ] Types listed in `:AlwaysMuted` / `:NeverMuted` are shown as disabled and can't be changed - [ ] Choices are saved to the user's account and still show after a reload - [ ] Muting a type stops the email and/or the in-app entry for that type, depending on which channel was muted - [ ] Existing list, dismiss and "Clear All Notifications" behavior is unchanged - [ ] An automated test checks that a muted type is saved and that the UI is hidden when `:ShowMuteOptions` is false

iqss.title: Feature Complete:  missing the Add "Replication Data for" to Title
iqss.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF puts an `Add "Replication Data for" to Title` button directly beneath the Title field on the create-dataset form. It is a one-click convenience for depositors publishing replication datasets: it prefixes whatever is in the Title with "Replication Data for: ". The new frontend's create-dataset form has no such control. ## Legacy JSF behavior `datasetFieldForEditFragment.xhtml` renders the button for the `title` field whenever `DatasetPage.editMode == 'CREATE'`. It is client-side only — clicking it prepends `dataset.replicationDataFor` ("Replication Data for:") to the current title value. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Start a new dataset: Add Data -> New Dataset, or `/dataset.xhtml?ownerId=1&editMode=CREATE`. 3. Observe the `Add "Replication Data for" to Title` button under the Title field. 4. Type a title and click the button; the title becomes "Replication Data for: ". ## New frontend behavior The SPA create-dataset form (`/modern/datasets/:collectionId/create`) renders the Title field with no adjacent button. A case-insensitive search for `replication` across `src/` and `public/locales/` returns no matches, so the affordance does not exist anywhere in the SPA. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Go to `/modern/datasets/root/create`. 3. Observe the Citation Metadata section: the Title field has no "Replication Data for" helper button. ## Expected behavior The create-dataset form should offer the same one-click way to prefix the title for replication datasets — or, if the team considers the affordance obsolete, the decision should be recorded so this inventory row can be closed deliberately rather than left as a silent omission. ## Current behavior Absent. Depositors must type the "Replication Data for:" prefix by hand, which is where the legacy button existed to keep the wording consistent across an installation. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy create-dataset form: the `Add "Replication Data for" to Title` button sits directly under the Title field. <img width="870" height="897" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac3595b7-42d0-4165-8680-13785277d245" /> ### New frontend SPA create-dataset form, same collection: Title has no helper button. (Note that "Host Collection" and "Edit Host Collection" *are* present here — two neighbouring rows in the missing-items list turned out to be implemented.) <img width="870" height="897" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8d1f931-3b43-4241-a98d-7827c4880d5d" /> ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/datasetFieldForEditFragment.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/datasetFieldForEditFragment.xhtml) (the `replicationDataButton`, rendered when the field is `title` and `editMode == 'CREATE'`), `dataset.AddReplication` and `dataset.replicationDataFor` in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: no match for `replication` anywhere under `src/` or `public/locales/`; the create form is [`src/sections/create-dataset/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/create-dataset) - Missing-items entry: "Dataset Metadata - Add Replication Data Prefix" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - No issue covering this affordance was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "replication data", "replication data for" and "title prefix" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The create-dataset form offers a one-click way to prefix the title with "Replication Data for: ", or the team records a decision not to carry the affordance forward - [ ] Clicking it prepends the prefix to the current title without clearing it, and does not duplicate the prefix when clicked twice - [ ] It appears only in create mode, as in legacy - [ ] Covered by an automated test if implemented

iqss.title: Feature Complete: Support contact or User Guide link
iqss.body: ## Summary Every legacy JSF page carries "User Guide" and "Support" links in the site header, and "Support" opens a contact form addressed to the installation's support address. The new frontend's header has neither — it shows only Language, Add Data and the user menu when signed in, or Language and Log In when anonymous. There is no way to reach installation support, or the user guide, from anywhere in the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dataverse_header.xhtml` renders "Add Data", "Search", "User Guide" and "Support" alongside the user menu. "Support" is a command link (`headerSupportLink`) that opens the shared contact dialog (`PF('contactForm').show()`), pre-addressed to installation support rather than to a specific collection. Both links appear on every page, including the account pages, and for anonymous visitors. ### Steps to observe 1. Open the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080). 2. Observe "User Guide" and "Support" in the top-right header, on any page — including Account -> Account Information. 3. Click "Support" and observe the contact form for installation support. ## New frontend behavior `Header.tsx` renders the brand, a `LanguageSwitcher`, and then either `LoggedInHeaderActions` (Add Data + user menu) or a single OIDC "Log In" button. Nothing else. The SPA does have a contact modal, but it is the per-collection "Email Collection Contact" reached from a collection's "Contact" button — that addresses the collection's contacts, not installation support, and it is not reachable from the account pages or from a dataset. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern), signed in or not. 2. Inspect the header: only Language, Add Data and the user menu (or Log In). 3. Go to `/modern/account?tab=accountInformation` and confirm there is no Support or User Guide link anywhere on the page. ## Expected behavior The new frontend should offer an installation-level support contact and a user-guide link that are reachable from any page, as legacy's header does — so a user who is stuck, or whose account details are wrong, has a route to ask for help. ## Current behavior Absent. The only contact affordance in the SPA is the per-collection "Email Collection Contact" modal, which has a different recipient and is not available from account or dataset pages. Users have no in-app path to installation support and no link to the documentation. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy Account Information page — note "User Guide" and "Support" in the header, present on every page. ### New frontend The same page in the SPA: header has only Language, Add Data and the user menu — no Support, no User Guide. (This capture also evidences jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#21, the read-only account table.) ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml) (`headerSupportLink` opening `contactForm`, and the User Guide link), `header.support` and `header.guide` in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx) and [`LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx) — no support or guide entry; the existing contact modal is [`src/sections/shared/contact/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/shared/contact) (collection-scoped) - Missing-items entries: "Account Information - Contact Support", and the related "Contact Support" rows under Login Page, ORCID Confirmation, OAuth Login Callback and Search Results in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#21 (Account Information is read-only) and #24 (notification muting absent) are the sibling account-area gaps; a user hitting either has no support link to fall back on, which is part of why this one matters. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#10 (no Sign Up entry in the header) is the other missing header affordance. - The collection-level contact form itself is fully implemented, including its math CAPTCHA — two rows of the missing-items list about that turned out to be wrong. This issue is specifically about an *installation* support route. - No issue covering a header support or user-guide link in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "contact support", "support link", "user guide link" and "header support" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] An installation support contact is reachable from any page in the new frontend - [ ] It addresses the installation's support address, distinct from a collection's contacts - [ ] A user guide link is available from the header, as in legacy - [ ] Both are available to anonymous visitors as well as signed-in users - [ ] Covered by an automated test asserting both are present in the header

iqss.title: Feature Complete: Link Search
iqss.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets an authenticated user save the current filtered search on a collection as a "linked search," attaching it to one of their own collections so the search results surface there too (similar to linking a dataverse). The SPA's equivalent "Link" menu only offers "Link Collection" — the search-linking option is absent entirely. ## Legacy JSF behavior On any collection page, the "Link" dropdown offers a "Link Search" action that opens a "Link Search" dialog. The dialog lets the user pick one of their own collections and save the current search against it via "Save Linked Search". ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as a user who owns at least one collection. 2. Navigate to any collection page (e.g. a collection with sub-items). 3. Click the "Link" dropdown button near the top of the page, then click "Link Search". 4. Observe the "Link Search" dialog, which lets you choose "Your Dataverse" and click "Save Linked Search". ## New frontend behavior The equivalent "Link" dropdown on a collection page in the modern frontend only exposes "Link Collection". There is no "Link Search" entry, so the save-linked-search workflow cannot be started at all. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as the same user. 2. Navigate to the equivalent collection page. 3. Click the "Link" dropdown button. 4. Observe that only "Link Collection" is offered; there is no "Link Search" option. ## Expected behavior The Link menu on a collection page should include a "Link Search" option that opens an equivalent "save the current search" dialog, letting the user attach the search to one of their own collections. ## Current behavior The feature is entirely absent from the SPA — not even a placeholder/"Not Implemented" modal is shown, since there is no menu entry to click in the first place. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Link Search" dialog, reachable from Link -> Link Search on a collection page. ### New frontend Modern frontend "Link" dropdown showing only "Link Collection", with no search-linking option. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: src/main/webapp/dataverse.xhtml (linkDataverseForm dialog), src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataversePage.java (saveSavedSearch(), linkMode) - New frontend source: no matching route/component found under src/router/routes.tsx or src/sections for this feature - Missing-items entry: "Dataverse Page - Save Linked Search" in DV - Missing items.md ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#546 ("Analysis and proposal for more customizable collection page") discusses displaying linked items on a customized collection page, but does not cover saving/creating a linked search. Not a duplicate. - No duplicate found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse, or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc after searching "save search", "linked search", and related terms. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The collection page's "Link" menu includes a "Link Search" option - [ ] Selecting it opens a dialog allowing the user to choose one of their own collections - [ ] Saving creates a linked search associated with that collection, matching legacy behavior - [ ] Covered by an automated or manual test verifying the linked search appears for the target collection

iqss.title: Browser tab title is static instead of reflecting page context
iqss.body:
## What steps does it take to reproduce the issue?

1. Open the React version of Dataverse.
2. Navigate between different pages/contexts: the home page, a collection page, a dataset page, a file page, the login page, search results, account page, etc.
3. Observe the browser tab title in each case.

## When does this issue occur?

On every page load/navigation in the React frontend.

## Which page(s) does it occur on?

All pages. Confirmed static on the home page (shows repository/root collection name regardless of context) and the login page (doesn't indicate you're on the login page). Based on the legacy JSF behavior, this likely affects every page type, including: collection pages (root and sub-collections), dataset pages, file pages, login page, account/profile page, search/advanced search, permissions management pages, dashboard/admin pages, and error pages (404/403/500).

## What happens?

The browser tab title never changes — it always shows a single static value (the repository/root collection name), no matter what page or object the user is viewing.

## To whom does it occur (all users, curators, superusers)?

All users — this is frontend routing/rendering behavior, not permission-dependent.

## What did you expect to happen?

The tab title should update dynamically per page/context, mirroring the legacy JSF app's behavior:

- Root collection (home) page: the collection's name alone (e.g., `Demo Dataverse`).
- Sub-collection page: that collection's own name alone (e.g., `Sub Collection`) — does not include the parent/root name.
- Dataset page: `{dataset title} - {parent dataverse name}` (e.g., `Replication Data for: Foo Study - Demo Dataverse`).
- File page: `{filename} - {containing dataverse name}` (e.g., `data.tab - Demo Dataverse`).
- Login page: `Log In - {root dataverse name}` (e.g., `Log In - Demo Dataverse`).
- Other pages (account, search, permissions, dashboard, error pages, etc.) generally follow `{action/page label} - {contextual or root dataverse name}` (e.g., `Advanced Search - Demo Dataverse`, `404 Not Found - Demo Dataverse`).

In the legacy JSF app, each page defines its own title via a `pageTitle` template parameter rather than one fixed value, so the pattern is not perfectly uniform across every page — but the general rule is: the tab title always reflects the current page/object, with the containing dataverse's name commonly appended for dataset/file/utility pages.

SPA User.
